items.summary: An article reports that Amazon is likely the biggest financial winner from Anthropic’s planned public offering, driven by convertible notes with $6.2 billion in principal outstanding as of June 30 and equity investments totaling about $18 billion per Amazon's filings. Because Anthropic’s private valuation reached $965 billion, small VC stakes yield billions while percentage ownership stays low. The S-1 warns that cloud providers like Google also build rival AI models.
items.title: Amazon Positioned as Largest Beneficiary of Anthropic IPO

items.summary: Poonam Gupta, deputy governor of the Reserve Bank of India, said in a Business Standard fireside chat that India would already be an 8% growth economy but for external shocks. She credited digital infrastructure and public services for resilience, noting the goal is to raise growth from around 7% to 8%. A better global environment could add another 50 basis points to one percentage point within a year.
items.title: RBI official says India would have hit 8% growth without global shocks

items.summary: South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix unveiled a shareholder return plan of about 100 trillion won (S$96 billion) for 2026, comprising cash dividends and share repurchases. The announcement follows a more than seven-fold rise in quarterly operating profit to a record high on Oct 28, driven by AI infrastructure demand lifting memory chip prices. SK Hynix reiterated it expects demand to exceed supply through 2030.
items.title: SK Hynix Announces S$96 Billion Shareholder Return Plan

items.summary: Tesla is nearing 1,000 vehicle registrations in India for 2026 after recording 990 between January and October 26, per Vahan data compiled by Flash Finance. It trails market leader BMW (4,014) but narrows the gap with Mercedes-Benz (~1,369). Tesla’s overseas shareholders infused ~₹86 crore in fresh equity during FY26, raising its Indian subsidiary’s capital to ~₹136 crore as it expands retail and service operations.
items.title: Tesla Approaches 1,000 India Registrations as Equity Infusion Backs Expansion

items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India is expected to release a consultation paper on relaxing rules requiring foreign portfolio investors with concentrated equity exposure or large asset size to disclose granular investor details. Proposed changes include exempting certain funds from additional requirements, though the Sebi spokesperson declined comment. The current thresholds trigger disclosure if over 50% of assets are in one company or group, or AUM reaches ₹50,000 crore.
items.title: Sebi May Relax FPI Investor-Disclosure Rules

items.summary: The Supreme Court acknowledged media’s freedom of speech but said it must be balanced with citizens’ right to privacy and dignity, asking petitioner Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) how the two rights could coexist. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymlaya Bagchi and V Mohana warned against misuse of press rights while protecting innocent citizens.
items.title: Supreme Court Asks Media Body To Balance Free Speech With Privacy

items.summary: Australia's food-sector annual inflation rose to 3.2% in the year to September 2026, while headline inflation reached 4.3%, sharpening expectations of a fifth Reserve Bank interest-rate rise before its 3 November decision with the cash rate at 4.6%. RBA officials say subdued growth is needed to control prices amid rising fuel and transport costs.
items.title: Australian inflation and politics as RBA weighs another rate hike

items.summary: Polls have closed in the Israeli election and votes are being counted, with BBC's Hugo Bachega reporting on what might happen next. Exit polls suggest Gadi Eisenkot's bloc won the largest number of seats but has not won a majority, while Netanyahu's Likud party is set to be the biggest single party in parliament.
items.title: Israeli election vote count underway after close

items.summary: In North Garland, Texas, Ashley Schmidt has stopped gardening and cycling because delivery drones emit an annoying buzz that triggers her fight-or-flight response; she says the sound is noticeable even indoors. Experts say low-altitude drone noise can be novel and intrusive to residents unfamiliar with aircraft sounds, and complaints may grow as services expand across roughly 500 US locations by Amazon Prime Air. The Federal Aviation Administration regulates commercial drones but points responsibility at operators and communities. Companies are responding: Greenjets claims a propulsion system that reduces noise by at least two thirds; Greg Sharrow's company developed tipless loop blades tested in water; an Amazon spokesperson says its latest propellers produce almost half the perceived sound of prior designs.
items.title: Drones buzz, so makers seek quieter designs

items.summary: A decade after the Paris Agreement, a new Lancet Countdown report says climate change’s health harms are worsening faster than before. Authored by 146 researchers from more than 30 countries and produced with the World Health Organization, it finds heat deaths reached an estimated 710,000 in 2023—more than HIV or malaria losses that year—with over 70 percent attributable to human activity. Harms fall hardest on lower-income nations. The authors urge WHO member states to declare climate change a global health emergency ahead of COP31. Quotes from Marina Romanello, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Diana Picon Manyari and Jeni Miller frame the urgency.
items.title: Lancet Countdown Warns Climate Health Harms Are Accelerating

items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Japanese leaders Tuesday (Oct 27) to safeguard the political foundation of China-Japan relations, per Xinhua. He extended condolences for former prime minister Yasuo Fukuda, who died at 90 last week and sought closer ties with China. The remarks marked a rare direct reference from Beijing since relations worsened after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi angered officials in November.
items.title: Xi Urges Japan to Protect Ties After Fukuda Death

items.summary: Japan's rising interest rates are pushing Kyoto Financial Group toward selling some of its stakes, which carry about $6 billion in paper gains. President Nobuhiro Doi said the lender could profit by converting shares to cash and lending it out, adding that strategic shareholdings should be reconsidered. The group has long held cross-shareholding positions in companies such as Nintendo and Kyocera.
items.title: Kyoto Financial Group weighs cashing in on cross-shareholding gains as rates climb

items.summary: Three months after a magnitude-7 earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture, killing 38 people and leaving 1,073 residents still sheltering as of Tuesday. The prefectural government reports 82,223 houses affected, with 11,429 destroyed or damaged; only one house has been demolished since demolition began last month. Evacuees have fallen from a peak above 10,000 to roughly one-tenth, while about 2,685 people occupy temporary housing and approximately 380 lost their jobs by Oct. 16.
items.title: Kumamoto Residents Remain in Shelters Months After Earthquake

items.summary: A State Department official, speaking on condition of anonymity due to visa privacy laws, said the department will issue visas to Flavio Bolsanaro and his family and allow them entry into the United States (s0). Bolsonaro had been under investigation in Brazil for corruption, money laundering and tax evasion and ordered to surrender his passport after losing the runoff election to Lula by a margin of nearly 4%, with Lula receiving more than 64 million votes versus fewer than 60 million for Bolsonaro (s18). The senator denied wrongdoing and framed the move as intimidation. A spokesperson for Argentina's Ministry of Security denied reports that he had entered the country, while his whereabouts remained unclear to reporters gathered outside his home in Brasilia (s32).
items.title: Bolsonaro Family Granted U.S. Visas Amid Brazilian Election Fallout

items.summary: Chinese officials say families are for the first time supporting more elderly people than children, with the dependent-elderly ratio rising to 23% in 2025 versus 22% for children. Figures from China's National Bureau of Statistics put those aged 65 and above at over 223 million (nearly 16% of the population) against about 213 million children aged 14 and under. Analysts say the shift strains pensions, healthcare and long-term care while reshaping spending.
items.title: China's Families Now Support More Elderly Than Children

items.summary: Research published in Tobacco Control found that AI bots flooded a 2023 UK government consultation on banning disposable vapes with tens of thousands of fake responses. The Department of Health and Social Care identified 90,835 machine-generated submissions out of 118,756 total replies (76%), most opposing the ban. These were excluded from decision-making; Labour passed the law in 2024.
items.title: AI Bots Flooded UK Vape Consultation

items.summary: South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix reported a more than seven-fold rise in quarterly operating profit to 83.3 trillion won for July-September, beating the 76.7 trillion won LSEG SmartEstimate as AI-driven demand lifted memory prices. The company said it will pursue about 100 trillion won ($75.4 billion) in shareholder returns this year through cash dividends and share repurchases. SK Hynix reiterated that demand is expected to exceed supply through 2030, citing long-term agreements with 14 major customers covering more than 50 per cent of production capacity for 2027 and 2028.
items.title: SK Hynix Unveils $75 Billion Shareholder Return Plan Amid Record Q3 Profit

items.summary: The BBC Radio 4 programme Tech Life presents a week of episodes covering several tech stories. It examines how the programming language PHP, little known over its more than a year online availability, has become widely recognised after vulnerabilities were discovered, with insiders telling the story of the resulting crisis. The series also reports on an AI avatar that took and retold a comedian's jokes to gain millions of views, and answers listener questions from UCLHPC director following a visit to the UK's national supercomputer.
items.title: Tech Life Explores PHP Crisis and AI-Generated Comedy

items.summary: SGTech's Gavin Chua and Gunasekharan Chellappan argue Singapore must invest in both artificial intelligence and quantum computing without waiting for either to mature. They note that AI adoption has already outpaced organisational readiness, with employees experimenting independently while companies struggle over structured rollout. Drawing on the Economic Strategy Review (ESR), they say success requires doing both well at once, pointing to how semiconductors were built through long-term investment before commercial outcomes were certain. Chua is Chairman of SGTech; Chellappan was former Chairman of its AI, Cloud and Data Chapter.
items.title: Singapore Should Invest in AI and Quantum Together Now

items.summary: The item is a single-line caption identifying an op-ed cartoon by Ella Baron about the autumn budget. No figures, quotes or claims appear in the text beyond that label, so it names only its subject and creator without further detail.
items.title: Op-Ed Cartoonist Takes Aim at Autumn Budget

items.summary: Crude oil held gains after a two-day decline, with West Texas Intermediate steadying near US$100 and Brent closing below US$114. The movement followed a tight Israeli election in which opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot edged ahead of Benjamin Netanyahu, shaping tense government talks. Traders also weighed Iran diplomacy, rising Middle East risks, falling US crude stockpiles reported by the American Petroleum Institute, and an upcoming Federal Reserve decision.
items.title: Oil Prices Steady as Traders Await Israeli Election Outcome

items.summary: In the first round of NEET-PG 2026 counselling, general medicine received more seat allotments than radiodiagnosis among top entries. General medicine led with 51 of the first 100 seats. Prof Neeraj Nischal of AIIMS noted that career choice should follow personal fulfilment rather than earning speed.
items.title: General Medicine Leads NEET-PG Round 1 Allotments in New Delhi

items.summary: Donald Trump announced his administration is terminating Biden-era methane regulations holding oil and gas companies accountable for large leaks during a rally in Lubbock, Texas. He said the change would save consumers and energy producers $45bn and unlock 210 million barrels of oil – equivalent to about 10 days of US petroleum consumption. Environmental Defense Fund's Rosalie Winn called it enabling worst polluters while wasting energy.
items.title: Trump Announces Termination of Methane Regulations

items.summary: Actor Noah Wyle was named this year’s “sexiest man alive” by People magazine on Tuesday (Oct 27). The 55-year-old said it “sounded like a prank,” adding he did not expect the honour. He joked about taking ribbing from friends and family, while noting his ER co-star George Clooney has received the title twice.
items.title: Noah Wyle Named People's Sexiest Man Alive

items.summary: A New York court sentenced Tal Alexander, 40, and his twins Oren and Alon to 30 years each after they were found guilty of drugging and raping dozens of women over decades. During the hearing, 12 victims spoke of lasting trauma, while prosecutors urged maximum punishment. The brothers' lawyers argued for shorter terms and maintained their innocence.
items.title: Alexander brothers jailed for decades in sex-trafficking case

items.summary: The MSCI Asia Pacific Index rose 0.6%, with benchmarks in Australia, Japan and South Korea advancing as optimism around the AI trade re-emerged after a recent chip-stock rout. Meta's $25 billion share sale was five times oversubscribed, while reports of large raises from Meta ($98 billion), SpaceX ($40 billion) and an Anthropic S-1 filing eased concerns about continued investment in the sector.
items.title: Asian Stocks Rise on Renewed AI Optimism

items.summary: Rating agency Icra expects bank credit growth to ease to 15-16% in full-year FY27 from the current 18-19%, noting a higher base may make gains look smaller. The agency also projects only marginal asset-quality deterioration and improving net interest margins as Reserve Bank of India hikes rates, without giving an FY28 credit estimate.
items.title: Icra Forecasts Slowing Credit Growth for FY27

items.summary: Petrol and diesel prices stayed unchanged across major Indian cities on October 28, though CNG rose in several places. New Delhi petrol sits at ₹102.12 with diesel at ₹95.20; Hyderabad leads petrol at ₹116.15 while Chandigarh is lowest at ₹101.54. Thiruvananthapuram tops diesel at ₹104.40, and Chandigarh trails it at ₹89.47. CNG climbed by ₹2 in Chennai, Mathura and Meerut, reaching ₹99.50 there.
items.title: Indian Fuel Prices Hold Steady as CNG Rises in Key Cities

items.summary: A Scroll investigation reports that India's government-backed ethanol program, launched in 2018 through biofuel blending mandates and the use of maize and sugarcane for fuel, has not delivered promised benefits to growers. Petroleum minister Hardeep Puri claimed it saved Rs 1,60,000 crore, with Rs 1,40,000 crore returned to farmers; Scroll found little ground evidence. Farmers in Chhindwara and Shamli say maize and sugarcane prices stayed below support levels, payments were delayed by months, and the shift toward rice-based ethanol dampened demand for corn. Experts from Arcus Policy Research attribute low prices to oversupply and policy unpredictability. The report notes a separate 2024 Economic Times account of an ethanol oversupply crisis, with capacity around 20 billion litres against roughly 11 billion litre needs.
items.title: India's ethanol push falls short of farmers' expectations

items.summary: Former Australian Open champion Stan Wawrinka ended his professional tennis career after losing in the first round of the home Swiss Indoors event in Basel to Jiří Lehečka. His final season concluded a career that began in 2002 and included three grand slam titles: the 2014 Australian Open, 2015 French Open, and 2016 US Open, each won against the then-world number one player.
items.title: Stan Wawrinka Ends Professional Tennis Career After Swiss Indoors Defeat

items.summary: Australia's annual inflation rose to 4.3 per cent in September, above expectations, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said. Housing added most, and fuel prices climbed 9.4 per cent monthly. The Reserve Bank targets 2-3 per cent. Bloomberg data put the chance of a rate hike next week at about 85 per cent. RBA deputy governor Andrew Hauser called inflation too high but broadly as expected.
items.title: Australia's September inflation surge raises rate-hike odds

items.summary: A new mapping by Amazon Underworld finds criminal networks or armed groups operate in nearly three-fifths of municipalities across six Amazon countries. Of 1,310 examined, illicit actors appeared in 768 (59%), with Colombia highest at 98%. About 78% of Colombia's rural population—nearly 10 million people—
items.title: Amazon Underworld Report Maps Criminal Networks Across Six Amazonian Countries

items.summary: A cyclonic storm, later named Arnab in one report, began landfall along the coasts of Andhra Pradesh and Puducherry's Yanam around Ongole and Kakinada. Officials expect the process to finish within two to three hours. Andhra deployed about 85,000 personnel and relocated residents across more than 1,500 locations; Odisha evacuated over 45,000 people, including more than 700 from Gopalpur. At least 21 flights were cancelled at Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam airports on Tuesday.
items.title: Cyclone Ornab Makes Landfall on Odisha and Andhra Coasts

items.summary: Shreyas Iyer led India to a record six-wicket victory over New Zealand in the third T20I at Wellington, as openers Abhishek Sharma (113) and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (45) chased down 199 in 13.2 overs — the fastest chase of a target above 190 by a Full Member nation. Iyer called their Powerplay display 'mind-boggling' and praised their adaptability, while India took an unassailable 3-0 series lead.
items.title: 'Ball was still seaming': Iyer 'mind-boggled' by Abhishek, Sooryavanshi's blitz

items.summary: The very severe cyclonic storm Cyclone Arnab is forecast to make landfall between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam on the Andhra Pradesh coast early Wednesday, with wind speeds reaching 125 kmph and gusts up to 140 kmph. Nearly 150,000 people have been moved to shelters across Andhra Pradesh and Odisha as rescue teams are deployed ahead of landfall. State governments reported evacuating about 90,000 in Andhra Pradesh and roughly 48,000 in Odisha by Tuesday evening, with further evacuation expected Wednesday morning. Chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu said saving lives is the priority and urged people to take precautions without panicking.
items.title: Cyclone Arnab Nears Andhra Coast as Nearly 150,000 People Evacuated

items.summary: The Supreme Court bench questioned the government Tuesday over its failure to bring all medicines under price control, citing a case where a distributor procured an anti-cancer drug for ₹1,100 but a private hospital charged ₹1.30 lakh. The court asked why economic interests should outweigh citizens’ lives and criticised the Centre’s decision to cap only 137 drugs at 30% of MRP as coming after its intervention. Solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati argued Indian drug prices are globally cheapest, while the bench warned policy may benefit corporates even as patients suffer.
items.title: Supreme Court Pressures Centre on Medicine Price Controls

items.summary: A very severe cyclonic storm, named Arnab, is forecast to complete landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast within four to five hours. The impact zone spans Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam, with wind speeds estimated between 125 and 150 kilometres per hour and gusts up to 180 kilometres per hour. Authorities have relocated residents across more than 1,500 locations and deployed nearly 85,000 personnel, targeting zero loss of life.
items.title: Cyclone Arnab Makes Landfall Near Kakinada as States Prepare for Storm Surge

items.summary: Research in Kashmir’s Sindh Basin identifies an elevation band of approximately 1,750-2,875 meters as a key zone where groundwater feeds springs. A 2023 University of Kashmir study linked spring decline to climate variability and land use; follow-up work mapped recharge areas using field surveys, GIS mapping and stable water isotope analysis. Residents Shafeeqa and Momin describe multiyear declines in their Cherwan village spring. Lead author Hilal Ahmad Sheikh says protecting the uphill landscape may sustain springs better than improving outlets alone. Hydrogeologist Suhail Ahmad Lone cautions that recharge maps are not exact boundaries, calls for long-term monitoring and field data before attributing decline to climate or human activity, and urges investment “uphill.” A July agreement between a watershed programme and the University of Kashmir aims to prepare spring-rejuvenation project reports.
items.title: Kashmir Spring Decline Points to Uphill Recharge Areas

items.summary: Israeli voters cast ballots in their highest turnout since 1999, the Central Elections Committee reported at 10 p.m. Tuesday — a rate of 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades. Early exit polls gave Eisenkot's opposition bloc 52 seats versus Netanyahu's coalition's 50, though no party won a majority of the 120-seat Knesset and final tallies were still being counted Wednesday. Analysts said an outright winner was unlikely, so forming a government could take days or weeks. Voters on both sides weighed in; one called it crucial while another doubted anyone could replace Netanyahu. Supporters at Likud rallies held out hope for their leader amid the ongoing war with Iran.
items.title: Record Israeli Election Turnout Boosts Opposition's Path Past Netanyahu

items.summary: Preliminary Israeli exit polls project an anti-Netanyahu bloc at 52–53 seats versus about 50 for the prime minister's allies, both short of the 61 needed for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. Likud stays largest with 24–25 seats; Yashar is projected second on 21–23. Supporters celebrated as projections appeared on screens, and Eisenkot declared victory, saying results gave him first right to form a government. Results remain preliminary, with weeks of coalition talks expected before confirmation.
items.title: Israeli Exit Polls Give Anti-Netanyahu Bloc Narrow Lead

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department said on Wednesday that very severe cyclonic storm Arnab remained practically stationary along the Andhra Pradesh coast, with its landfall process expected to continue for another 2-3 hours. The IMD placed the system's centre near latitude 16. 4 degrees north and longitude 82 degree east, close to Narsapur, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, forecasting maximum sustained winds of up to 135 kmph with gusts reaching 150 kmph over the next three hours. Rainfall exceeding 200 mm was recorded across Anakapalli, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam districts between 8. 30 am on October 27 and 4 am on October 28, topping out at 261. 5 mm in Kannuripalem. Police rescued four stranded people near Bombay Katta in Kakinada, while the School Education Department converted 609 schools into rehabilitation centres holding 854 people as of 5. 50 am on October 28.
items.title: IMD Warns Cyclone Arnab Landfall To Continue For Hours

items.summary: US Rep. James Comer (R-Ky.) wrote Delaware Governor Matt Meyer urging documents on a proposed Artificial Intelligence Company, warning it could shield owners from liability for reckless or harmful actions and enable anticompetitive capture. The draft bill would let AICs pursue any lawful purpose except banking, with AI agents managing the business in a 30-month regulatory sandbox. Comer said he may propose federal legislation to limit state authority.
items.title: Delaware’s AI-run company plan draws legal-oversight pushback

items.summary: Thousands of demonstrators gathered outside Portugal's parliament on Tuesday evening in Lisbon, protesting the housing crisis and alleged police violence during camp-clearing operations. Singer Marisa Liz joined the rally, where protesters chanted against fascism. President António José Seguro called for dialogue while awaiting investigation results. Demonstrators oppose easier evictions and rent caps.
items.title: Lisbon Protesters Rally Against Housing Crisis and Police Violence

items.summary: Back-to-back encounter killings, custodial deaths and public parading of accused have raised concerns over due process and police accountability in Bengal. Two men shot dead by police within hours—Prahlad Das in Gaighata on October 26 and Samiul Sheikh in Dhulian—and the death of undertrial Basudeb Naskar at Baruipur Subdivision Hospital on October 27 have drawn scrutiny, with the cause of death still to be established. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari’s earlier advocacy of an Uttar Pradesh-style encounter model during the 2023 panchayat campaign has intensified criticism from opposition parties and rights groups such as APDR, who warn that political endorsement blurs lawful policing with punishment outside courts. Police accounts remain unverified by independent investigations.
items.title: Bengal Sees Rise in Encounter Killings and Custodial Deaths Amid UP-Style Policing Fears

items.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's current Ebola outbreak, the fastest spreading in history and the largest ever by geographic scope from Nigeria to Kenya, has surpassed 10,000 infections since being declared in May, per government figures. It ranks second only to the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak in deaths (nearly 5,000 versus over 11,000). Katie Thomas-Canfield of the International Rescue Committee called the rapid pace staggering and attributed delays partly to U.S. aid cuts. The Bundibugyo species drives transmission amid community distrust; roughly 80% of new cases come from people off health officials' radar, keeping the outbreak out of control as no licensed vaccine or treatment exists for this strain.
items.title: Congo's Fastest-Spreading Ebola Outbreak Passes a Grim Milestone

items.summary: Exit polls project an anti-Netanyahu bloc at 52–53 seats versus about 50 for the prime minister's allies, both short of the 61 needed to win a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. Likud stays largest with 24–25 seats; Yashar is projected second on 21–23. Eisenkot declared victory and said he has the first right to form a government, though results are preliminary and weeks of coalition talks remain before any prime minister is confirmed.
items.title: Israeli Opposition Supporters Celebrate Narrow Lead in Exit Polls

items.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro, son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro and a right-wing senator under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering, left Brazil for the United States Tuesday despite a court order banning him from exiting. He holds Italian nationality since 2023. His campaign manager Rogerio Marinho said he had received only one text message before losing contact. Defeated by Lula with 51.8 percent of the vote, Bolsonaro called the exit ban a scare tactic and pledged to lead opposition.
items.title: Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro Flees to US After Election Loss

items.summary: Early Wednesday exit polls from major Israeli TV stations suggested a hung result, with Netanyahu’s bloc and Gadi Eisenkot's each winning about 51 seats while Arab parties won about 18. The outcome would trigger weeks of coalition jockeying before a prime minister is named or another election called — the country’s first national vote since Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023 attack. Eisenkot said the polls show a “lack of confidence” in Netanyahu and vowed to form a government; final results may vary. Voter turnout reached more than 77%, the highest since 1999.
items.title: Israeli Exit Polls Show No Clear Winner in Netanyahu Referendum

items.summary: Industry leaders tempered criticism of rising energy demand from AI, data centers and electric vehicles with optimism about grid modernization. At TechCrunch Disrupt, executives from WeaveGrid, Veir and Rewiring America highlighted new opportunities in load orchestration and infrastructure upgrades. Veir's superconductive cables reportedly carry power five times farther using 20 times less space, while the company raised $110 million earlier this month.
items.title: AI Surge Sparks Grid Modernization Optimism at TechCrunch Disrupt

items.summary: A family's lawyer said a 59-year-old man who died on Oct. 17 in Paris may have succumbed to tear gas exposure, following an autopsy that found acute cardiorespiratory failure and opened a judicial investigation. The family filed a complaint against police over alleged intentional violence resulting in death without intent to kill. The prosecutor's office said the man had a pre-existing heart condition; further forensic analyses are requested as the case continues.
items.title: Family files complaint over tear gas role in protester's death

items.summary: The EU is lobbying G7 nations to increase support for Ukraine, according to the item's lead sentence, as Non-EU allies have pledged only $4.5 billion for 2027, per the Financial Times reported, down from more than $20 billion this year amid a global cost-of-living crisis. France's Marine Le Pen called new funding before April elections a democratic scandal.
items.title: EU Urges G7 Nations to Boost Ukraine Funding Amid Expected Drop

items.summary: Just days after Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Sunday's Brazilian presidential election, Flávio Bolsonaro fled Brazil for the United States, according to official U.S. sources and associates of the far-right leader. Figures close to him acknowledged the move to Folha de S. Paulo after he defied a court order from Supreme Federal Court justice Alexandre de Moraes to surrender his passports within 24 hours over alleged involvement in an online gambling money-laundering scheme. U.S. officials confirmed the plane was heading there, and reports indicate the Trump administration will grant him asylum.
items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro flees Brazil for asylum in United States

items.summary: Sam Wollaston argues that Britain's growing fridge disposal problem stems from climate change and hotter summers. Many standard UK fridge-freezers are rated only to +32C, below indoor temperatures during heatwaves. He calls for higher regulatory standards requiring manufacturers to produce durable appliances rated for tropical or subtropical conditions, warning otherwise landfill waste will keep rising.
items.title: Readers Link UK Fridge Disposal Crisis To Rising Summer Heat

items.summary: At GitHub Universe, a developer describes wearing a Game Boy Color–based conference badge that functions as a full color-screen computer. Working with Steve Francia, who used Gemini to build an NES emulator and then added emulators for the Game Boy and Game Boy Color, he says running The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening requires obtaining the ROM. He notes the badge can be flipped upside down to use built-in touch controller buttons on its body.
items.title: GitHub Developer Runs Zelda Emulator on Conference Badge

items.summary: Reuters reported that in 2025 the United States consumed about 48,000 tonnes of rare earth permanent magnets but produced only about 300 tonnes domestically, underscoring a supply gap China's export controls and new September 15 State Council regulations on skilled departures have widened. The Pentagon has prepared for life without Chinese rare earths through January 1, 2027 sourcing rules, though the Defense Department accounts for less than 0.1% of global demand per the U.S. Government Accountability Office. REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY) is building what it calls the largest heavy rare earth metallization facility outside China and announced roughly 150 tonnes per year of NdPr capacity in early 2027, while estimating its platform could eventually supply about 10% of ex-China dysprosium and terbium oxide demand. The IEA projects non-Chinese supply would meet only a fraction of expected magnet demand by 2035. RTX Corporation reported third-quarter 2026 sales of $25 billion with a record backlog, Lockheed Martin cited $20.7 billion in sales, L3Harris Technologies generated $5.9 billion and GE Aerospace saw orders surge 49% to $19 billion as defense manufacturers confront the same exposure.
items.title: U.S. Rare Earth Magnet Production Lags Far Behind Demand

items.summary: The White House offered a visa to Flávio Bolsonaro, per Semafor’s first report Tuesday, as the Trump ally reportedly fled to the US to evade corruption charges after losing Brazil’s presidential election. Analysts noted his defeat tests Washington’s “Donroe Doctrine” amid Latin American shifts toward Venezuela and Cuba.
items.title: US Offers Visa as Flávio Bolsonaro Flees Corruption Charges

items.summary: Anthropic, an AI firm valued at US$1 trillion (S$1. 3 trillion), is pursuing a stock market debut after five years of rapid growth. In its Oct 26 prospectus it warns that model differentiation may narrow, with substantially all revenue from AI tools and no advertising or cloud business to fall back on. Shareholders had floated a valuation of US$2 trillion but slowed quarter-on-quarter growth from 145% in the second quarter to 45% in the third, cooling expectations to around US$1. 5 trillion. The article identifies three threats: commoditisation as open models such as Kimi K3. 1 Pro close behind paid ones like Claude Opus 5.
items.title: Anthropic’s record IPO faces three threats as rivals catch up and prices fall

items.summary: The Information reported Tuesday that OpenAI is planning to buy Google's AI chips, citing a person familiar with the matter. The report disclosed no financial terms or details. It would deepen ties between the two rivals despite competing in AI products and search. Both companies declined comment; Google did not respond outside business hours.
items.title: OpenAI reportedly plans purchase of Google AI chips amid surging demand

items.summary: The Information reported on Tuesday that OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips, citing a person familiar with the matter. The report did not disclose financial terms or other details. Google and OpenAI both declined comment outside regular business hours. The announcement comes as Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet plan up to $600 billion combined this year in AI infrastructure spending amid investor skepticism about returns.
items.title: OpenAI reportedly planning purchase of Google AI chips

items.summary: The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region's Center for Food Safety decided on Tuesday, October 23, 2026, to suspend imports of poultry meat and products from Lolland Municipality in Denmark and Jackson County in Minnesota, US. The move followed notifications about highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza outbreaks. A CFS spokesperson said the decision protects public health, with trade instructed to stop importing immediately.
items.title: Hong Kong Suspends Poultry Imports Over Avian Flu Outbreaks

items.summary: Excess funds with Indian lenders fell from a September high of 11 trillion rupees ($116 billion) to 462 billion rupees by Oct. 26, per a Bloomberg Economics index, amid RBI measures defending the rupee at a near-record low. Analysts at IDFC First Bank and Emkay Global Financial Services expect tightness to persist as liquidity replenishment stays limited. Certificate of deposit rates rose about 40-50 basis points last week to a seven-month high.
items.title: RBI tightens liquidity as rupee nears record low, draining lender reserves

items.summary: Apple launched its new 14-inch MacBook Pro with an M6 chip, claiming up to 30% better graphics performance and a 24-hour battery life. The model starts at ₹2,39,900 in India, with pre-orders opening on October 28, 2026.
items.title: Apple Launches MacBook Pro M6 in India

items.summary: Apple introduced its new 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by the M6 chip, part of an upgrade to its professional laptop lineup aimed at demanding workloads such as software development and video editing. The machine keeps the Liquid Retina XDR display but centers on the processor for heavier applications. Apple frames the launch around whether these changes justify the price.
items.title: Apple launches M6 MacBook Pro in India

items.summary: Paris Smaragdis, an MIT professor with joint appointments in the Music and Theatre Arts program, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, and the Schwarzman College of Computing, researches machine learning for sound perception. He aims to help machines hear and understand audio as well as humans do, citing applications like locating traffic accidents by tire sounds or detecting drill failures underground. Smaragdis joined MIT in 2025 after a career at Mitsubishi Electric Research Labs, Adobe, and the University of Illinois. His group focuses on tools for musicians and flexible signal processing techniques.
items.title: MIT Professor Paris Smaragdis Advances Machine Hearing Research

items.summary: Anthropic, the maker of Claude, filed to go public in the US. The article highlights four Indian-origin executives: CFO and CTO Krishna Rao, Claude Code co-creator Rahul Patil, Sid Bidasaria, and Neil Buddy Shah, who chairs its Long-Term Benefit Trust. Anthropic reported $16.3 billion in first-half 2026 revenue versus $1.16 billion a year earlier, though net loss widened to $80.7 billion while operating loss narrowed to $693 million from $2.1 billion.
items.title: Anthropic Files for US IPO as Four Indian-Origin Executives Take Center Stage

items.summary: Anthropic published its IPO prospectus, which Finshots summarised for readers. The company earns money through usage-based payments and subscriptions; in FY25 it made $4.5 billion in revenue, over 1,000% more than the previous year, rising to $16 billion in the first half of FY26, up around 1,300%. Roughly 80% comes from usage-based payments and 20% from subscriptions. Despite this growth, Anthropic posted an operating loss of $8 billion and a net loss of $41 billion in FY25; its operating loss narrowed to $693 million but the net loss reached $80 billion in the first half of FY26, partly due to a $72 billion accounting adjustment. Finshots notes that underlying operating economics appear improving while risks include limited shareholder control and revenue concentration.
items.title: Finshots Breaks Down Anthropic’s IPO Prospectus

items.summary: A joint Bihar and Andhra Pradesh police team arrested two youths, Aditya Pandey (23) and Raja Kumar (24), at the Indo-Nepal border town of Raxaul for allegedly relaying One-Time Passwords to Pakistani intelligence operatives. SDPO Manish Anand led the raid that seized two phones with forensic evidence linking suspects to money transfers tied to Case No. 0-01/2026, from which Vijayawada investigators arrived on October 25 after tracking digital footprints.
items.title: Bihar and Andhra Police Arrest Two in Raxaul Over WhatsApp Espionage Ring

items.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to roughly 60,000 employees across the US, Canada, the UK and India at level 70 and below. Chief people officer Amy Coleman announced the Voluntary Exit Offer in a Monday memo, with no age or tenure requirement and decisions due by early December. Eligibility rests on team participation rather than individual choice; AI, Copilot, Windows, Xbox, finance and HR teams qualify fully, while sales, marketing and security do not. Accepting employees exit at year's end for up to 39 weeks of salary plus stock vesting and career support, but without the extended healthcare in the spring program. This is Microsoft's second buyout of 2026 following layoffs that cut about 4,800 jobs in July alone. The company says it expects fewer takers than the earlier retirement offer and insists this does not signal further job cuts, though a spokesperson noted future offers may follow business need.
items.title: Microsoft Extends Voluntary Exit Offer to Indian Staff

items.summary: Google began rolling out a built-in audio recorder in the Gemini Notebook mobile app on Android and iOS, starting October 27. Recordings last up to one hour and are stored as transcripts that become queryable sources within a notebook. Google first announced the feature on September 15. Creators Toolbox summarized details from Google's help center, noting no required plan or language limit is stated.
items.title: Google Rolls Out One-Hour Audio Recording in Gemini Notebook

items.summary: Google DeepMind released Genie 4 in research preview, describing it as its most realistic and interactive world model yet. The system generates photorealistic worlds with built-in audio—music, ambient sounds and dialogue—and lets users change scenes live via text or image prompts. Built on Gemini Omni, a scene stays consistent for up to two minutes. It is available now to trusted testers through Project Genie but remains closed to the public.
items.title: Google DeepMind Releases Real-Time AI World Model Genie 4

items.summary: Reliance’s Jio Platforms shares rose 21% in their Mumbai debut on Oct 28, giving India’s biggest-ever initial public offering a strong start and making it the second-largest company by market capitalisation in India at about US$131.52 billion (S$168.6 billion), ahead of Bharti Airtel and HDFC Bank. The listing marks Reliance Industries’ first sale after two decades, as Ambani pursues an “everything company” strategy across consumer and technology sectors.
items.title: Jio Platforms Shares Jump After Record Indian IPO Debut

items.summary: Former Supreme Court judge Sanjay Kishan Kaul said pre-trial detention has become 'punishment' in India, commenting on bail denials to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam. He argued that prolonged proceedings can punish people before conviction or acquittal, and that bail should generally be the norm.
items.title: Ex-SC Judge Kaul Calls Pre-Trial Detention a Punishment in India's System

items.summary: BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal are in advanced negotiations to revive their alliance ahead of the Punjab assembly elections, though seat-sharing and accommodating rebel faction Punar Surjit remain unresolved. The parties' equation has shifted after SAD's decline since 2020 and BJP's gains; sources say BJP's share could nearly double from its usual 23 seats in the 117-member House. Home Minister Amit Shah says the NDA will win, while Badal signals openness to other partners. The alliance is seen as their best shot at power amid rising Hindu-Sikh harmony concerns and Waris Punjab De's challenge.
items.title: BJP and Akali Dal Resume Seat-Sharing Talks Before Punjab Polls

items.summary: Israeli exit polls show Benjamin Netanyahu's governing bloc tied with the opposition grouping led by Gadi Eisenkot on 51 seats each, short of the 61 needed to form a majority coalition government. Final counting is ongoing as parties begin negotiations that could take weeks.
items.title: Israel Exit Polls Show Netanyahu and Eisenkot Blocs Tied

items.summary: The National Trust of Australia (Victoria) announced that a ginkgo biloba in Geelong’s botanic gardens won 2026 as Victoria’s tree of the year, beating eight finalists with 27% of 4,435 public votes. Planted in 1859 and standing about 20 metres tall, it is the largest ginkgo in the state and a popular wedding backdrop. National Trust executive manager Justin Buckley called it “a very popular winner” while urging stronger statutory protection for significant trees, which he said remain inadequate. Botanic gardens supervisor Sheree Parker described it as the park’s most visited tree after years of dormancy.
items.title: Geelong ginkgo named Victoria’s tree of the year

items.summary: The Australian federal government has advanced a digital duty of care bill through the House of Representatives, aiming for passage by end 2026. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese framed it around children treating chatbots as their best friend and urged the Coalition to support it. The Greens back the law; the Coalition opposes it while Labor seeks its backing amid possible amendments. Accepted changes would ban AI conduct simulating emotional intimacy that fosters a child's dependence on it, requiring platforms to offer algorithm opt-outs. Communications minister Anika Wells rejected claims of censorship as an Orwellian slogan. The bill now moves to the Senate, where Greens and independent MPs push for external complaints mechanisms and expanded powers for the telecommunications industry ombudsman.
items.title: Australia's digital duty of care bill would ban AI emotional intimacy

items.summary: The 2026 Light of the Internet Expo opens in Wuzhen from November 2 to 5 as part of the World Internet Conference (WIC) Wuzhen Summit. Now in its 12th edition, this year's theme is 'Intelligent Connectivity, Smart Future,' and it will showcase next-generation connectivity, computing, large models, intelligent devices, industry applications, smart living and cybersecurity across six zones. Organizers have prioritized satellite internet, quantum communication, 6G and ultra-wideband.
items.title: Wuzhen Expo Opens With 6G, AI Agents and Robots Focus

items.summary:
Syria reopened its main border crossing with Jordan on Wednesday (Oct 28), as the two countries reaffirmed ties strained by a deadly retaliatory strike from Jordanian forces. The raid followed gunmen opening fire during a Greek Orthodox church funeral in Karak, killing nine people and wounding 25. Syria condemned it an "unacceptable violation," while Jordan said it killed more than 20 militant fighters. A joint security committee will meet to discuss operations against IS. Damascus denied coordinating with Amman over the raids.

items.title: Syria Reopens Jordan Border Crossing After Mending Ties

items.summary: Singer Demi Lovato reassured fans she is 'fine' after sharing a now-deleted Instagram Story showing an IV and hospital wristband. She suggested sushi or passionfruit may have triggered the reaction, writing: "I'm either allergic to passionfruit or sushi now!" A source told TMZ that Lovato was discharged shortly after being evaluated and her symptoms subsided quickly.
items.title: Demi Lovato Reassures Fans After Hospital Visit Over Possible Allergic Reaction

items.summary: Japan's Nidec may not obtain an auditor's opinion on its securities report by month-end after PwC Japan said the audit would not be completed in time. The Nikkei business daily reported this without citing sources. Nidec will submit internal control documents to the Tokyo Stock Exchange by the deadline while seeking early review of listing maintenance, and it announced plans to sue founder Shigenobu Nagamori and eight former executives over suspected accounting irregularities.
items.title: Nidec May Miss Audit Deadline, Nikkei Reports

items.summary: Macnica, a Japanese cybersecurity company, reported that cyberattacks on publicly accessible websites and apps have more than doubled from last year, reaching 216 cases of confirmed or suspected data breaches so far this year—about 2.6 times the prior total. A government official said AI was likely being used to make attacks easier.
items.title: Japanese cybersecurity firm reports surge in AI-driven website attacks

items.summary: In Hong Kong, artificial nest boxes are giving the critically endangered yellow-crested cockatoo refuge and research access in a city where storm damage and tree pruning have eliminated more than 60% of natural nesting hollows. Astrid Andersson of the University of Hong Kong calls it “a housing crisis for these birds.” Biologist Harry Wong built camera-fitted boxes with her, installing 15 across parks since March 2025; four are occupied and one chick was successfully raised.
items.title: Nest boxes give Hong Kong’s rare cockatoos shelter amid hollow shortage

items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping extended condolences on Tuesday to the family of former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda, who died. Describing him as a statesman known for integrity and responsibility, Xi said Fukuda was committed to China-Japan friendship and upheld correct views of history. During his tenure he signed the fourth political document between China and Japan. Xi expressed hope that Fukuda's family would carry on his legacy.
items.title: Xi Jinping Extends Condolences Over Death of Japan's Former PM Fukuda

items.summary: The Villa Vie Odyssey suspended its years-long world voyage after fuel costs surged. Its operator said monthly cabin fuel prices rose to as much as $8,000 (£6,000) from $1,800. Around 200 passengers were ordered off in Cambodia. The company will spend the next 60 days restructuring and recapitalising, though no outcome is assured.
items.title: Luxury Cruise Ship Suspends Voyage Over Fuel Costs, Stranding Passengers in Cambodia

items.summary: The bereaved family of Murat Cicek, a Kurdish man who died in custody at a Tokyo police station on July 2, has sued the Tokyo Metropolitan Government and his contract doctor. Filed Tuesday with the Tokyo District Court, the suit seeks ¥57 million ($361,000) in damages. The complaint alleges the doctor overlooked a bowel injury and that staff left him untreated despite symptoms.
items.title: Kurdish Man's Family Sues Tokyo Government Over Custody Death

items.summary: A government wildlife rescue center in Khon Kaen, Thailand reports annual leopard cat admissions rising from about 10 cats per year before 2023 to as many as 65 now. Staff treat burns and infections before rehabilitating kittens over two months for soft release into Phu Pha Man National Park. Mortality rates dropped to around 33% in 2026, from 60% previously. Local forests are nearing capacity, prompting studies of other areas.
items.title: Thai Center Rescues Injured Leopard Cat Cubs

items.summary: In a Free Press column excerpt, the author frames artificial intelligence hacking risks as a worst-case scenario rather than an expectation. He argues that current systems use varied protections and would likely prove more robust than feared, shifting toward post-quantum methods even at great cost. The columnist notes math breakthroughs may arrive in stages, giving time to adjust.
items.title: Columnist Frames AI Hacking Risks as Worst-Case Scenario, Not Prediction

items.summary: At the 2026 Financial Street Forum in Beijing, global asset managers said debate over Chinese assets has shifted from whether to allocate to how to allocate well. Regulators pledged broader and more predictable market opening. At a CSRC roundtable on Oct. 21, executives from GIC, Amundi, Allianz Global Investors and JP Morgan Asset Management discussed long-term opportunities amid geopolitical conflict, technological change and climate concerns. Michael Krautzberger of Allianz called China the closest rival to the US in AI. Li Yimei of China Asset Management stayed bullish over three pillars. Travis Spence highlighted Chinese bonds as a portfolio stabilizer. According to CSRC data, Chinese listed companies posted revenues of 37.7 trillion yuan ($5.65 trillion) and net profits of 3.6 trillion yuan, up 19.5% year-on-year in the first half of the year, with dividends and buybacks totaling 2.1 trillion yuan. Participants said global capital is entering a new phase of systematic re-pricing of Chinese assets.
items.title: Global Asset Managers Recalibrate China Allocation at Beijing Forum

items.summary: Tayla Lee Brailey, a former high school teacher in Sydney, was sentenced to 15 months in prison after pleading guilty to four charges relating to sexual offences against two teenage students in 2024. Judge Elizabeth Ryan said the breach of trust warranted custody and ordered her onto the NSW Police child protection register for 15 years.
items.title: Former Sydney teacher jailed for sex acts with students

items.summary: Football Australia says it is monitoring security in the Middle East ahead of two Socceroos friendlies, one against Qatar in Doha and another against Jordan in Amman. The matches are scheduled next month as final warm-ups before January's Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia. Recent regional violence has raised concerns, but FA says it expects the games to go ahead.
items.title: Football Australia expects Middle East friendlies to proceed

items.summary: Asian tech shares rose on SK hynix's blockbuster third-quarter results, with operating profit up 632% to US$62. 8bn (€54. 2bn), the firm said Wednesday after six straight records of strong revenue and profit from advanced semiconductor demand. The gain added to AI optimism following Anthropic's IPO filing showing about 1,300% first-half revenue growth and a reported US$63bn financing structure for new capacity announced Tuesday by Broadcom with Citi, Blackstone and Morgan Stanley. SK hynix shares climbed almost 9%, while South Korean rival Samsung added more than 8%.
items.title: SK hynix profit surge lifts Asian tech stocks amid AI optimism

items.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy revealed on Tuesday that Ukrainian forces, in an operation codenamed Veles carried out by the National Guard's 2nd Khartiia Corps near Kupiansk, infiltrated Russian positions through underground gas pipelines. He said more than 100 Russian troops had been eliminated and over 30 captured. Zelenskyy described transforming a tactic previously used against Ukraine.
items.title: Ukraine's Underground Pipeline Operation Near Kupiansk

items.summary: Residents of the Villa Vie Odyssey, a cruise ship stranded without fuel off Sihanoukville after running out of diesel during an around-the-world voyage that began in October 2024, were ordered to disembark by 2 p.m. on Tuesday, villa owner Mikael Petterson said. About 200 residents remained aboard the 650-passenger vessel when the order came. Villa Vie Residences says fuel costs have risen sharply since the Iran War began and is seeking new funding within 60 days while covering lodging but not travel out of Cambodia.
items.title: Villa Vie Odyssey Residents Ordered Off Stranded Cruise Ship in Cambodia

items.summary: The United States says it will issue visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family, even as reports say he may have left Brazil after losing the presidential election by more than four million votes. His whereabouts are not independently confirmed. He lost to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva while refusing to concede.
items.title: U.S. To Issue Visas to Flávio Bolsonaro Amid Unclear Whereabouts

items.summary: Jio Platforms shares jumped 21% on their Mumbai debut, valuing the company at $108.3 billion and marking Reliance Industries’ first listing in two decades. The stock opened at 1,358 rupees a share versus its 1,119-rupee offer price. Jio’s telecoms business serves more than 530 million customers. Brokerages called the valuation attractive but flagged competition and regulatory changes as risks.
items.title: Jio Lists at Record $3.2 Billion in India IPO

items.summary: Exit polls from Israel’s election, reported by Al Jazeera, showed a neck-and-neck race between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and rival Gadi Eisenkot. Neither bloc was projected to win the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member Knesset; Arab-led parties were expected to take 18 seats. Final results are due Friday.
items.title: Israel Exit Polls Show Netanyahu Bloc Neck-and-Neck With Rivals

items.summary: South Korea has completed development of a domestically produced marine attack helicopter under a project costing about 450 billion won, roughly $337 million. The aircraft is based on the KUH-1 Surion platform and adds air-to-ground missiles plus systems to counter enemy helicopters and drones. It passed combat suitability evaluation in July and received airworthiness certification in August. Local media reported that production of around 20 helicopters will begin in 2027, according to DAPA.
items.title: South Korea Finishes Indigenous Marine Attack Helicopter Development

items.summary: As nearly 42% of votes were counted, Netanyahu's bloc was projected to win 57 seats—four short of the 61 needed for a majority. The opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot was expected to take 47 seats, while Arab parties could hold balance with 16. Figures remain provisional and may change as counting continues, per The Times of Israel citing the Central Elections Committee.
items.title: Netanyahu Bloc Falls Short of Majority in Israeli Vote Count

items.summary: Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated that India's mobile phone manufacturing sector generated Rs 25,000 crore in direct tax collections, exceeding the Rs 19,000 crore paid out under its production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme. He added the programme contributed Rs 3,000 crore in GST and said electronics manufacturing employs 25 Lakh people while mobile manufacturing alone employs 12 Lakh. Vaishnaw dismissed reports questioning the model as he pushed for a new Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme approved by the Union Cabinet in July with Rs 62,500 crore allocated to run from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31.
items.title: Vaishnaw Defends Mobile PLI Scheme on Tax and Jobs Grounds

items.summary: The BJP won four of the six counted seats in Uttar Pradesh’s Legislative Council election, while the Samajwadi Party (SP) took one. The ruling party led in Gorakhpur Teacher and Agra Graduate; the SP was ahead across Varanasi Graduate, Agra Teacher, Lucknow Graduate and Jhansi Graduate. Counting for six remaining seats continued on Wednesday under single transferable vote procedures that began Tuesday at 8am. An Opposition candidate boycotted counting in Gorakhpur over alleged irregularities, saying votes suddenly swung to the BJP rival by about 450 votes. The SP had won three of 11 council seats in 2020, when the BJP held six and independents two. Congress-SP alliance later polled 43.52% of votes for its 43 assembly seats in 2024.
items.title: BJP and SP split Uttar Pradesh council seats as counting drags on

items.summary: According to StockEdge's technical scan data, seven stocks in the Nifty200 index had closing prices that crossed above their 200-day moving averages on October 27, 2026. The 200-day moving average is a widely used indicator for gauging overall trend direction; when a stock's price stays above it on the daily timeframe, it typically signals an uptrend.
items.title: Seven Nifty200 Stocks Cross Above Their 200-Day Moving Averages

items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government announced a revision of auto-rickshaw fares, doubling the minimum base fare from 25 rupees to 50 rupees for the first 1.8 kilometres and raising the per-kilometre rate from 12 rupees to 25 rupees. The change follows long-standing demands and multiple protests by the Auto Drivers Association after more than a decade of campaigning.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Doubles Auto-Rickshaw Minimum Fare Amid Cyclone Michaung

items.summary: India reportedly invited Pakistan's Heritage and Culture Minister Aurangzeb Khan Khichi to the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum, set for New Delhi from November 20 to 22. All ten member states were extended invitations by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who announced the event in Dushanbe on October 20 amid ongoing India-Pakistan tensions following Operation Sindoor in May 2025.
items.title: India Extends SCO Civilisation Forum Invitation to Pakistan

items.summary: Videos show waves breaching the coast and trees uprooted as cyclonic storm Arnab hit Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. The India Meteorological Department said the powerful 'very severe' storm remained practically stationary along the Andhra Pradesh coast after its northern spiral band moved inland, bringing heavy rain, strong winds and flooding to districts across both states.
items.title: Cyclone Arnab Lashes Odisha and Andhra with Waves, Uprooted Trees

items.summary: In Karnataka's four-seat Legislative Council poll, the BJP-JD(S) opposition alliance won all seats: JD(S) took Bengaluru Teachers' Constituency from Congress via A P Ranganath by 908 votes (10,810 to 9,902), while BJP held its three segments. The outcome was seen as a sign of opposition consolidation and not expected to affect the Congress government's stability.
items.title: Opposition Alliance Sweeps Karnataka Legislative Council MLC Polls

items.summary: Stock market benchmarks Sensex and Nifty tumbled in early trade on Wednesday, dragged by IT companies, rising crude oil prices and caution ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy decision. The 30-share BSE Sensex dropped 601.14 points to 72,997.55; the 50-share NSE Nifty fell 146 points to 22,604.80. Brent crude traded higher at USD 115.4 a barrel.
items.title: Indian benchmark indices fell sharply on Wednesday amid rising crude prices

items.summary: The proposal to extend Bengaluru’s Namma Metro Yellow Line from Bommasandra in Karnataka to Hosur in Tamil Nadu has drawn strong public support, according to a ground report by The Federal Karnataka. IT employees, students and auto drivers say the line would ease severe traffic congestion along stretches such as Attibele and Electronic City. In 2023, Karnataka’s IT and Biotechnology Minister Priyank Kharge raised objections that lower costs in Hosur could lure Bengaluru industries across the border; however, some industry associations did not share those concerns. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay appealed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for approval. The estimated cost is around Rs 6,900 crore, and final clearance still depends on several factors.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister appeals for Bengaluru-Hosur Metro extension

items.summary: Plaid Cymru ministers want extra cash for Welsh railways and public services ahead of the UK government's Wednesday Budget. Finance Minister Elin Jones asked Chancellor John Healey to treat Wales fairly, requesting £1bn of promised rail funding be brought forward and help with the 2027-28 budget facing a real-term cut. She said Wales had been short-changed for years. Extra spending on devolved services in England could bring additional funds to Wales. Meanwhile, shoppers at Swansea Market cited cost of living as their top concern ahead of the announcement.
items.title: Plaid Cymru demands more funding as UK Budget approaches

items.summary: At a campaign rally in Lubbock, Texas on Tuesday night, President Donald Trump announced his administration would terminate the Biden-era methane regulations. The Environmental Protection Agency proposed relaxing monitoring and emission-control requirements after complaints from the oil and gas industry, which called the rules an economic threat. Environmental groups warn that weaker restrictions will worsen air pollution near operations. Experts note stripper wells produce more than half of the industry's emissions yet account for only 5 percent of output. Darin Schroeder of the Clean Air Task Force said marginal producers are not necessarily marginal polluters, and let them off the hook would significantly impact climate change efforts.
items.title: Trump's EPA rolls back methane rules

items.summary: Next week's gubernatorial elections could shift energy and environmental policy across many states, according to Inside Climate News analysis drawing on election forecasts from Sabato's Crystal Ball at the University of Virginia. Democrats are favored to retain governorships in Arizona, Michigan, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin, while also poised to take control from Republicans in Alaska, Iowa and Ohio. Analysts note that Democratic governors with unified legislative majorities have enacted more ambitious climate laws, as seen when Illinois' JB Pritzker gained a trifecta after his 2018 victory. Experts emphasize the governor's power over utility commissions and appointees can determine energy direction, especially amid high prices and scrutiny of bills. Wisconsin, Alaska and other closely contested races draw particular attention because winners could reshape commission membership or data center rules. The article notes that party control alone is insufficient where legislatures remain divided or regulators are elected rather than appointed. A quotation from Dylan Reed underscores the governor's central role in state energy policy over utility costs.
items.title: Governor Races Could Reshape State Energy Policy

items.summary: A ceasefire that began in Oleshky has been extended across the wider Kherson region, according to sources who helped broker it. US First Lady Melania Trump said on Tuesday that the area had expanded to provide safe passage for humanitarian convoys, a claim later corroborated by Ukraine's public ombudsman press secretary and deputy head of Kherson Oleksandr Tolokonnikov. The truce will be followed by aid deliveries and an evacuation planned for Friday. Residents report severe hunger amid no food or electricity since the 2023 Kakhovka Dam breach, while escape routes remain mined. Ukrainian officials warn evacuees may end up in Russia rather than Ukraine.
items.title: Ceasefire Extended Across Kherson Region for Humanitarian Aid

items.summary: Oil prices rose in early Asian trade as renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia revived supply concerns, with Brent futures at $115.70 per barrel up 1.62% and WTI at $101.20 per barrel up 1.34%. The Houthis claimed a ballistic missile hit the Ras Tanura refinery, though Saudi authorities have not confirmed damage or operational interruption. Falling inventories estimated by the American Petroleum Institute added support while reports of an impending U.S. campaign against Iran reinforced upward momentum.
items.title: Houthi Strikes on Ras Tanura and U.S. War Rumors Push Oil Higher

items.summary: Marry Mubaiwa, the former wife of Zimbabwe's vice-president Constantino Chiwenga, was released from remand after about seven years while her husband faced an attempted murder trial. Charged in 2019 over claims she tried to impede his medical treatment in South Africa, she had been denied bail and suffered prejudice during proceedings. A magistrate ordered the release citing mental, physical and financial harm; the state sought a one-month postponement to engage witnesses.
items.title: Ex-wife of Zimbabwe's vice-president freed after seven years on remand

items.summary: Tech Life, a BBC World Service programme presented by Chris Vallance and produced by Imran Rahman-Jones, previews its next episodes. It tells the story of the PHP crisis after vulnerabilities were discovered that made the acronym widely known. The show also features an interview with a comedian whose jokes were retold by an AI avatar that gained millions of views online, plus questions answered by the director of the UK's national supercomputer following an earlier visit.
items.title: BBC Tech Life programme covers PHP crisis and AI story

items.summary: India has invited all ten SCO member states, including Pakistan, to its inaugural Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi from November 20-22. Officials said the multilateral invite is unrelated to bilateral ties but should be read within broader SCO collaboration. The forum was proposed by PM Modi at the Tianjin summit and organised by India's Culture and External Affairs ministries.
items.title: Will Pakistan's minister visit Delhi? India invites Islamabad first time after Operation Sindoor

items.summary: The government-backed Warm Home Loans scheme launched Tuesday, offering UK households interest-free or low-interest loans of £7,500 to up £35,000 to fund heat pumps, batteries and solar panels with no upfront cost. Energy suppliers British Gas and E.On partnered with lenders to offer the loans directly. The government says installing these technologies could save households up to £550 a year on energy bills. The scheme runs within a £2.7bn five-year budget that Treasury officials plan to cut, reportedly because they consider it a subsidy used mainly by middle-class households.
items.title: UK Warm Home Loans Scheme Launches for Solar and Heat Pump Upgrades

items.summary: Shaktikanta Das, RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta, said India is in striking distance of 8% growth. He cited macroeconomic stability, continuing structural reforms, and strategic policy initiatives developing domestic capacity as the triple engines powering it. Das highlighted the BFSI sector's role in supporting next-gen Digital Public Infrastructure, green finance, and financial inclusion on the path to a high-income economy.
items.title: RBI's Shaktikanta Das sees India near 8% growth on reforms and stability

items.summary: South Korea's media regulator fined Google and Apple a combined 63.71 billion won (S$61 million) on Oct 28 for forcing developers to use their in-app payments and delaying reviews, under a 2021 law. The Korea Media and Communications Commission imposed 42.9 billion won on Google and 20.81 billion won on Apple after concluding the conduct harmed competition and left developers with little choice.
items.title: South Korea Fines Google and Apple Over App Store Practices

items.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman accused opposition leader Rahul Gandhi of repeatedly decried the successes of Indian industry and now trying to incite business leaders to spread distrust. She said her government values enterprise as a job creator and driver of economic growth. The remarks followed a dispute within Tata Group over reappointing N Chandrasekaran, which Noel Tata challenged.
items.title: Sitharaman Counters Gandhi on Tata Remarks, Calls Him Cowardly

items.summary: The Nifty IT index fell more than 3%, leading sectoral losses, while South Korea's Kospi rose 6% after SK Hynix reported a seven-fold profit jump and planned to return about $75 billion to shareholders. Peer Samsung Electronics shares advanced nearly 9%. Indian firms Mphasis and Infosys each dropped 5%, with others falling around 3% or 1%. Analysts note India's 'anti-AI' advantage, though investor Michael Burry warns of a possible crash if the AI boom fades.
items.title: Indian IT stocks fall as global AI trade rebounds

items.summary: OpenAI intends to buy AI computing chips from Google, per a person familiar with private discussions who asked not to be identified. Final terms are unknown. The move supports OpenAI's efforts to expand its AI infrastructure amid a broader industry push toward homegrown chips challenging Nvidia.
items.title: OpenAI Plans to Buy Google’s Chips as Part of Its AI Build-Out

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke of the Cockroach Janata Party accused the Centre on Wednesday of a digital crackdown, saying removing posts and accounts would not resolve public grievances. He posted on X that takedowns could erode trust with citizens. The remarks follow wider scrutiny of content restrictions under Section 69A, court notices over suspended handles like @bring_back__ballot, and hearings scheduled for November 6.
items.title: CJP Founder Blames Centre for Instagram Content Takedowns

items.summary: Residents of a Southaven, Mississippi neighborhood have received offers from xAI to sell their homes as part of Elon Musk’s AI expansion. Real estate agents reportedly went door to door offering purchases tied to not joining the noise lawsuit filed by three locals in June over unpermitted gas turbines. Gavin Foust predicts more sales will follow. The EPA has found the turbines operated without federal permits, and environmental groups sued to stop their use. xAI denies all claims, stating it intends to be a good neighbor while building what Musk calls the world’s largest cluster of AI supercomputers.
items.title: xAI Buyout Offer in Colonial Hills

items.summary: On October 28, Amazon.com unveiled five new Alexa-powered devices, including a redesigned Echo Show 16 with a 16-inch screen, Fire TV, and night-vision camera priced at $499.99, alongside an Echo Studio speaker ($249.99), a smart Echo Dot hub ($99.99), the sleep-sensing Echo Time clock ($199.99), and the Alexa Photo Frame (from $199.99). The launch comes as Amazon faces growing competition from Apple, which recently introduced HomeView at $299 and the HomePod mini 2 at $149.
items.title: Amazon Unveils Redesigned Echo Show and New Alexa Devices

items.summary: Mukesh Ambani, 69, was emotional as four generations of the Reliance dynasty rang the opening bell at Jio Platforms Ltd’s stock market debut. His children spoke to investors about family unity and a value horizon for the next 50 years. The stock rose 21 per cent on its first day, making the group India’s most valuable conglomerate in rupee terms as it surpassed Tata Group.
items.title: Ambani Family Rings Bell at Jio Listing

items.summary: Apple is expected to unveil its first touchscreen MacBooks at a Los Angeles event on Wednesday, ending years of resistance to touchscreens. The launch caps recent product releases ahead of the holiday season. Analyst Anshel Sag said Apple was always wrong about touch and that change feels inevitable.
items.title: Apple Set to Debut Touchscreen MacBooks in Product Push

items.summary: The Korea Media and Communications Commission fined Google 42.9 billion won ($32 million) and Apple 20.8 billion won ($15.5 million), citing a violation of the 2021 law barring app store operators from forcing developers to use specific payment systems. The commission ordered both companies to allow external payment links, improve review procedures, and stop charging a 26% commission that effectively forced in-app payments.
items.title: South Korea Fines Google, Apple Over App Store Payment Rules

items.summary: A Tesla Semi caught fire on Interstate 880 in Hayward, California, Tuesday evening with no crash reported. The electric truck's lithium-ion battery burned long enough to keep the southbound freeway closed about 10 hours; CHP cited potential hazardous chemical smoke and reopened all lanes around 3:30 a.m. Wednesday. The driver exited unhurt, and the cause is under investigation. This was the second Tesla Semi fire in California to close an interstate in roughly two years, following one on I-80 near Emigrant Gap where NTSB found impact preceded ignition. Analysts note truck fires are common overall but stress that a no-crash self-ignition warrants scrutiny as volume production ramps up.
items.title: Tesla Semi Fire Closes I-880 for Hours With No Crash

items.summary: Threat intelligence firm Defused reported on October 27 that attackers were probing systems unpatched against a critical, recently disclosed Oracle E-Business Suite vulnerability (CVE-2026-101767), which allows remote code execution. Although Oracle has not confirmed exploitation in the wild, it urged immediate patching after reports of successful intrusions targeting customers who failed to apply updates. Shadowserver tracks over 670 exposed instances, mostly US-based, without confirming how many remain vulnerable.
items.title: Defused Reports Attackers Scanning for Recently Patched Oracle Flaw

items.summary: Jio Platforms made its National Stock Exchange debut, listing at ₹1,358 per share, a premium of over 21% to its IPO price of ₹1,119. With a market capitalisation of approximately ₹12.5 lakh crore, it became India's second-most valuable listed company behind Reliance Industries. The event drew attention for emotional family moments as Mukesh Ambani watched his sons speak about their legacy.
items.title: Jio Platforms Debuts at Record Price as Ambani Family Celebrates

items.summary: The Delhi High Court has sought the stand of the Centre and Meta Platforms in a plea against blocking the Instagram handle 'Bring Back Ballot', operated by Mission Save Constitution. On October 27, Justice Amit Mahajan issued notice to the petitioners and listed the case for hearing on November 6. The petitioner alleges that withholding an account with over 50,000 followers was disproportionate and unreasoned.
items.title: Delhi HC Seeks Centre, Meta Stand on Blocked 'Bring Back Ballot' Account

items.summary: Moneycontrol reported that Noel Tata, chairman of the Tata Trusts, is set to step down from six major Tata Group company boards on November 12, when he turns 70. The move follows the conglomerate's retirement policy for non-executive directors. He will remain a Tata Trusts nominee director at Tata Sons amid an ongoing dispute over N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as chairman.
items.title: Noel Tata Set to Leave Six Tata Group Boards

items.summary: Reserve Bank of India Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said on Tuesday that India's real GDP growth could have exceeded 8% without external shocks over the past three years. Speaking at a media summit, she noted growth stayed above 7%, and estimated better global conditions might add another 50 basis points to one percentage point.
items.title: RBI Deputy Governor Gupta Says India's GDP Could Have Crossed 8%

items.summary: Raúl Sánchez de la Sierra explains how armed groups in eastern Congo, where around 250 operate (s0), supply security, justice, taxation, and markets that an absent state cannot. Drawing on more than 15 years of fieldwork (s4) and records from one large militia with about 3,300 members (s27), he notes the group raises $1–2 million a month (s31). He also documents organised corruption in Kinshasa's traffic police, where bribes form only around a third of revenue (s47) and a quota system drives most income. Recruits scored higher than civilians on prosociality measures (s45), and 60% of district civilians say joining the militia is morally right (s38). Sánchez de la Sierra argues that policies ignoring these equilibria can backfire, advising researchers to rehumanise their social science rather than treating groups as mere criminals (s59-s62).
items.title: A Researcher Shows How Congo's Militias and Police Fill a Weak State

items.summary: A 2026 study by the BRAC Institute of Governance and Development examined how enumerator gender affects reporting of intimate partner violence (IPV) among women enrolled in Bangladesh's Ultra-Poor Graduation programme. Using a randomized design that assigned male or female enumerators to IPV questions, it found women reported substantially more abuse—particularly sexual violence—to female than to male interviewers: 27% versus 9%. The gap altered impact estimates; pooling data masked the programme's effect on emotional and dowry-related abuse seen in the female enumerator subsample. Researchers recommend gender-matched enumerators for sensitive surveys, noting the finding may apply beyond IPV.
items.title: Enumerator Gender Skews IPV Reporting in BRAC Study

items.summary: As jet fuel prices sit near double their pre-war levels, airlines are winding down or abandoning fuel hedging programmes and warning of steep fare increases. AirAsia's CEO Tony Fernandes said most hedging is finishing and carriers will be exposed to rising costs. Finnair stopped adding new hedges while budget carrier Norwegian was forced to undo price hikes because customers refused to pay more. Analysts say European fares rose 5.8% year-on-year in September, with US fares up over 20%. Ryanair's CEO Michael O'Leary expects air fares to rise by 15% to 20%, while Air New Zealand called fuel the single largest area of uncertainty.
items.title: Airlines Drop Fuel Hedges as Iran War Drives Fare Jumps

items.summary: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Wednesday, Oct 28, criticised Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi over remarks about the Tata Group.
