Responding to Gandhi's claim that the conglomerate was being 'criminally destroyed,' Sitharaman said casually labelling commercial and legal matters as criminal is unacceptable. She urged him to refrain from politicising every issue.
items.title: Sitharaman Calls Gandhi's Tata Remarks Unacceptable Over Politicisation Allegations

items.summary: Brazilian incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won his fourth presidential term in a Sunday runoff, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro with more than 64 million votes to just under 60 million. Analysts credit the turnaround partly to roughly 14.1 million additional voters who turned out for the second round. Lawmaker André Janones of Minas Gerais led Lula's Army, a WhatsApp channel that grew to nearly 11 million followers and shared pre-written messages, hashtags, and tasks with supporters. Data from Projeto Brief showed Lula reached 200 million social media interactions since October 5 versus Bolsonaro's 54 million, up from roughly equal figures at the campaign launch on August 16.
items.title: André Janones and Lula's WhatsApp Campaign Machine

items.summary: Anthropic acquired solo-run startup Mithril Medicine and began pursuing in-house drug discovery for two rare muscular dystrophies, Anthropic said. The work is mostly preclinical, with candidates yet to be tested in people. Founder Cody Tranbarger now works at Anthropic and intends to launch additional programs; if successful, a drug could enter human trials as early as late 2028.
items.title: Anthropic Launches In-House Drug Discovery After Acquiring Mithril Medicine

items.summary: Wall Street is preparing for what could become the three biggest initial public offerings in history as SpaceX has gone public and Anthropic and OpenAI are expected to follow. Doubts grow over whether these AI labs can generate enough value from their heavy spending; Anthropic lost more than $8 billion last year on $4.6 billion of revenue, while OpenAI projects a cumulative cash burn of nearly $280 billion despite expecting revenue to rise almost tenfold by 2030.
items.title: AI labs may build value others capture, analysts warn

items.summary: Lim Boon Wah wrote in a forum post that the National University Hospital should reconsider its plan, announced on Oct 27, to stop offering plastic bags at pharmacies from November. He argued patients discharged late may struggle to find packaging for expensive or perishable medication, and warned donated bags might be unavailable while paper ones cannot protect against rain.
items.title: Forum urges NUH to reconsider plastic bag ban at pharmacies

items.summary: A Forum contributor, Tang Min Hui, says Singapore's plan to raise the retirement age to 65 and re-employment age to 70 in 2029 can give older workers more ways to stay active. She argues continued work offers purpose beyond income but depends on real choices about contribution. Employers could use a voluntary experience-to-contribution pathway, inviting staff to describe specific incidents that might lead to coaching or quality-check roles rather than lighter duties alone.
items.title: Singapore Explores Turning Senior Work Experience Into New Roles

items.summary: Amazon announced a redesigned Echo Show 16 with a 16-inch screen, built-in Fire TV and night-vision camera. It is available for preorder starting at $499.99 or $569.99 with an anti-glare screen, shipping in December per Bloomberg. Amazon also introduced the Echo Dot, Echo Studio with Home Camera, Echo Time clock and Alexa Photo Frame, all running the latest Alexa.
items.title: Amazon Unveils Redesigned Echo Show 16 and New Alexa Devices

items.summary: Cockroach Janata Party founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged the Centre is directing Instagram to remove thousands of critical posts and accounts daily under the IT Act. Other creators, including Varun Grover and Deshbhakt, reported similar restrictions on satirical content. Dipke argued censorship would deepen distrust rather than silence dissent.
items.title: CJP Leader Alleges Government-Ordered Instagram Takedowns of Critical Posts

items.summary: The 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Convention on Biological Diversity in Yerevan has entered its final stretch, having adopted 14 decisions and secured more than $1.8 billion in financial commitments. It marks the first global review under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework's 23 targets for 2030. Schomaker of the Secretariat noted nearly 90% of parties set national biodiversity targets, while Andersen of UNEP stressed multilateralism continues to deliver. Divisions persist over funding responsibility and implementation; ministers attend the final week to break deadlocks on resource mobilization. The proposed Yerevan Pathway now guides priorities for the next two years as negotiators weigh long-term results over statements made in Yerevan.
items.title: COP17 Reaches Progress Amid Funding Divides as Negotiators Face Final-Week Hurdles

items.summary: Researchers at Shanghai Chenshan Botanical Garden identified two new sage species, Salvia zayuensis and Salvia toxantha, from the Hengduan Mountains. The discovery brings China's native genus total to 94, according to the garden. One was found in Zayu County during a 2019 expedition; the other in Songpan County in August 2023. Both were confirmed through physical and chloroplast DNA analysis, published recently in PhytoKeys.
items.title: Two New Sage Species Discovered in China's Hengduan Mountains

items.summary: In his first budget as chancellor, Healey announced a £100 energy payment this winter for households in council tax bands A to D. The move aims to help 20 million households cope with rising bills amid Middle East conflict. Healey also raised the minimum wage by 3.9% and extended VAT relief on electricity bills through July.
items.title: Healey's Budget Announces £100 Energy Payment for Millions of Households

items.summary: In his rape and sexual assault trial, Russell Brand told jurors he could not find anyone willing to give evidence on his behalf after the September 2023 Sunday Times, Times and Channel 4 Dispatches investigation. Prosecutors challenged his account of a 1999 hotel encounter in Bournemouth and questioned his past behaviour.
items.title: Russell Brand Testifies No Witnesses Could Support His Rape Defence

items.summary: Two trains collided just south of Madrid on Wednesday morning, killing at least 30 people with the toll expected to rise. The high-speed Renfe train reportedly rear-ended a stationary Iryo train near Mora and Orgaz around 09:00 (08:00 GMT). More than 500 passengers were believed aboard both trains; government spokesperson Esther Padilla cited 146 on the Iryo train plus one baby, and 397 on the Renfe train. Eighty people are being treated for injuries. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called it a serious accident and cancelled public engagements as emergency services respond.
items.title: Spain Train Collision Leaves at Least 30 Dead

items.summary: Adam McKay and Philip Eubanks argue that framing humanity's survival around an either-or choice between artificial intelligence and the climate crisis distracts from who actually controls the future. They contend both threats stem from a small group of private corporations, billionaires and political enablers making decisions to enrich themselves at public expense. Citing a Nature study, they note oil majors have allied with tech firms to use AI for exploration, potentially adding up to 1. 8 gigatonnes of carbon dioxide—equivalent to Russia's annual emissions—to the atmosphere. They point to community resistance: Data Center Watch counted at least 120 US datacenter projects worth nearly $200bn blocked or delayed in the first half of 2026 across 49 states, and Heatmap News found at least 20 canceled outright in the first three months alone.
items.title: McKay and Eubanks Reject AI or Climate as Humanity's End

items.summary: Toxic chromium in borewell water has left around 400 residents of Dattanagar, near the Ambad industrial estate on the outskirts of Nashik city in Maharashtra, with painful skin conditions. A laboratory test commissioned by SANDRP found total chromium at 50.5 mg/L, mostly hexavalent chromium, more than 1,000 times the permissible limit; a separate MPCB analysis found 45 mg/L, about 900 times the limit. Residents report itching, bleeding wounds and stigma, spending ₹5,000 to ₹6,000 a month on treatment or rent for clean water. Activists say untreated effluent may reach the Godavari before its 2027 Kumbh Mela; officials dispute this, citing depth and new sewage plants. A promised effluent treatment plant remains unbuilt after court orders.
items.title: Chromium Poisoning in Nashik's Dattanagar Neighbourhood

items.summary: A recent study found that most Important Shark and Ray Areas (ISRAs) in Indian waters along the Bay of Bengal fall outside marine protected areas, leaving breeding and nursery habitats vulnerable. Rhino rays are the world’s most threatened marine fish: over 70% of assessed species are considered threatened under IUCN, with about 15 listed in India’s Wildlife Protection Amendment Act 2022. Fisheries remain their largest threat.
items.title: Indian Rays Face Uncertain Future as Key Habitats Stay Unprotected

items.summary: At least 64 people have died and 80 were injured after an AVE high-speed train collided with a stopped Iryo train near Urda station in Toledo, Spain. The government said the toll may rise further. According to initial analyses from technical experts, an operator at Madrid's Atocha control center mistakenly ordered the Renfe train forward while the Iryo blocked the track; when the automated safety system failed and switched to manual mode, about eight trains stopped but the Iryo could not move, causing a rear-end collision at a speed yet to be determined. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said emergency services are assisting victims in coordination with authorities. Former labor minister Fátima Báñez was among those aboard; her condition is unknown.
items.title: Spain Rail Crash Kills at Least 64 in Toledo

items.summary: The Ebola outbreak has surpassed 10,000 people infected since its declaration in May, according to the latest figures from the Democratic Republic of Congo. This outbreak has spread faster than any in history and is also the largest in geographic scope, spanning from Nigeria to Kenya. It is second in death toll with nearly 5,000 deaths, around one-third of whom have been children. NPR's Daniel Estrin noted that Israelis went to bed thinking Eisenkot had the advantage, but by morning Netanyahu pulled ahead. Election officials expect to finish counting votes by tomorrow afternoon, and if no bloc secures a majority, it could take days or weeks for party leaders to form a governing coalition. The leading candidate will have six weeks to assemble support, likely competing for defectors across camps as Eisenkot's camp remains hesitant over mistrust of Arab parties after the Oct. 7, 2023 attacks.
items.title: Ebola Outbreak Passes Grim Milestone in Africa

items.summary: The article examines how Donald Trump increasingly praises the physical attributes—arms, shoulders, hands and faces—of Republican allies during the campaign for next Tuesday's midterm elections. Political communication experts consulted by EL PAÍS USA Edition argue these remarks should not be read as homoerotic but rather as a strategy to emphasize masculine leadership tied to national strength. Daniel Cassino of Fairleigh Dickinson University offers two explanations: Trump departs from conventional political language to sound authentic, and he exploits beliefs that masculinity equals good leadership for electoral gain. Kelly of the University of Nebraska likens Trump repeating these jokes to artists replaying an old hit.
items.title: Trump's praise of male physiques as political strategy

items.summary: A report warns that a powerful, record-strength El Niño will drive carbon dioxide levels higher this year. Warm Pacific waters trigger heat and drought, wildfires, wetland loss, and reduced ocean absorption while natural systems absorb less of human emissions. In 2025 concentrations hit record highs but rose less than in the 2024 El Niño. Ko Barrett said it "sets the stage for another surge." Experts note these effects remain hard to forecast.
items.title: Strongest El Niño in Memory Set to Push Carbon Dioxide Higher

items.summary: Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said on Wednesday there had been no breaches of the US-brokered local ceasefire around the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky during its first 30 hours. The agreement, held until November 1, lets residents evacuate from near-uninhabitable frontline conditions.
items.title: Melania Trump-brokered local ceasefire holds for second day in Oleshky

items.summary: AVEVA frames newer industrial systems as living digital twins that pair machine autonomy with human control, according to chief product officer Rob McGreevy. He likens adaptive models to organisms and says agentic AI is moving beyond diagnostics toward small adjustments that keep plants healthy—while operators still define what counts as healthy and flag misalignment. A 2026 Manufacturing Leadership Council survey found 66% of manufacturers use or plan agentic AI, with 40% expecting some factory autonomy by 2030; a Deloitte 2025 survey put operational risk among executives' top concerns at 65%. Nestlé reports Nesquik plants cut energy use by 16%, and SCG Chemicals cites 99% plant reliability. McGreevy expects AI to stay advisory for the foreseeable future, with full autonomy limited to narrow tasks, as governance guardrails take shape.
items.title: AVEVA Partners on AI-Driven Living Digital Twins for Industry

items.summary: As partial results emerged from Israel's parliamentary election, analysts said neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor his rival Gadi Eisenkot is set to win a majority. Netanyahu's Likud became the largest single party, with his bloc appearing just short of 61 seats in the 120-seat parliament. Analysts caution that early counts skew toward right-wing areas and that thousands of absentee ballots remain uncounted for another day or two. Eisenkot would likely need Arab-led parties to reach a majority, which most Jewish opposition parties have pledged not to do. Both leaders addressed supporters overnight pledging to form the next government as coalition talks begin.
items.title: Israel's election leaves Netanyahu and Eisenkot without clear majorities

items.summary: Alessandra Biffi, chief of paediatric haematology at Padua University Hospital in northern Italy and a former director of the gene therapy programme at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in Boston, is researching using DNA alteration to treat common conditions such as diabetes. She leads Immunostem, whose first phase began months ago. Biffi says the range of treatable diseases is growing toward non-inherited conditions affecting many people.
items.title: Gene therapy expands beyond rare diseases

items.summary: A high-speed train struck the rear of a stopped train Wednesday morning, derailing two cars and killing at least 30 people near Urda and Los Yébenes in central Spain's province of Toledo, according to local media. Spanish authorities had first reported 10 deaths; spokeswoman Esther Padilla said the toll would surely rise as state agency EFE later confirmed at least 30 dead. The crash involved RENFE and IRYO trains heading from Madrid toward Seville, making it the deadliest in Spain since an 80-fatality accident in 2013. Rail service was suspended across a wide region while emergency services responded to the wreckage.
items.title: Train Collision in Toledo Kills at Least 30

items.summary: Host country Turkey unveiled the Antalya AI Pledge, a voluntary commitment framing artificial intelligence as both an environmental risk and potential climate solution. The initiative will be presented at this month's summit in Antalya but lacks binding accountability mechanisms.
items.title: Turkey Launches AI Climate Pledge at COP31 Amid Data Center Emissions Concerns

items.summary: A Tehran court sentenced Iranian director Jafar Panahi in absentia under a new ruling, reportedly to five years and one month in prison plus asset confiscation. The verdict followed a December 2025 conviction for propaganda against the regime that carried a one-year term and two-year travel ban. His lawyer said he was not notified of the hearing; Panahi returned from Cannes on 30 March.
items.title: Tehran Court Sentences Palme d'Or Director Panahi in Absentia

items.summary: Rosie Llwellyn-Jones, a London-based historian specialising in the rulers of Lucknow and the 1857 Uprising, has published new likenesses of Hazrat Mahal for the first time. The images were discovered recently; few personal details exist in available records, so her portrait remains partly speculative. Llwellyn-Jones argues that despite her significant role during the uprising against British rule, Begam Hazrat Mahal was long a shadowy and almost forgotten figure. She confronted the East India Company after it annexed Awadh on February 11, 1856, defended her underage son Birjis Qudr as regent, and kept the company at bay for nearly a year before dying in 1879. The book runs 273 pages and costs Rs.799; one reviewer questioned its production quality.
items.title: Historian revives forgotten rebel Begam of Awadh

items.summary: Scientists say a rapid decline in Antarctic sea ice since 2016 has triggered a sharp salinity increase in the Southern Ocean’s Antarctic Intermediate Water, which extends from 2,300 to 4,000 feet deep. Co-author Bishakhdatta Gayen said the study combined six independent datasets spanning 2004 to 2024 and that the layer spreads northward into the Indian, Pacific and Atlantic oceans. Michael Meredith of the British Antarctic Survey added that if the low sea-ice state persists, these changes will ripple across global climate and ecosystems, though he noted it is not yet clear whether the shift is permanent given the short observational record.
items.title: Antarctic Sea Ice Loss Is Reshaping Global Ocean Circulation

items.summary: Blogger Adam Nash shares a post about household wealth inequality by age, drawing on recent US Census data cut by age. He notes that households aged 65 to 69 have a median net worth roughly nine and a half times that of those under 35, prompting students to blame Baby Boomers for hoarding wealth. Using an imagined equal society where everyone earns $100,000 annually, saves 10%, earns 8% on savings, spends 4% in retirement from ages 25 to 64 and lives to 85, he shows that age alone still produces large gaps through compounding. Nash cautions that most real-world inequality is within-age rather than between-age.
items.title: Adam Nash Explains Why Age Drives Household Wealth Gaps

items.summary: According to analysis by Avnet Silica, equity funding into the European solar sector reached €82 million ($91.2 million) by end August 2026, up from €24 million across all of 2025 and partway toward a projected year-end total between €90-100 million. Harvey Wilson said PV recycling led segment funding at €35 million, while 93% went to early-stage companies amid rising median rounds of €15 million. He cautioned the trend signals selective investing rather than full market recovery.
items.title: European solar startups raise €82 million in January-August

items.summary: A cyclone with winds of 125 kilometers per hour struck India's southeastern coast on Wednesday, October 28. Authorities warned of localized flooding and damage to power and communications poles. At least 180,000 people have been evacuated.
items.title: India Evacuates Over 180,000 as Cyclone Strikes East Coast

items.summary: A local ceasefire began Tuesday in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky and held through its first day and night, despite continued fighting between Moscow and Kyiv elsewhere. The truce is expected to remain in place until Sunday.
items.title: Ceasefire Holds in Occupied Oleshky for First 30 Hours

items.summary: At the October 28, 2026 Screen Music Awards in Brisbane's Fortitude Music Hall, West Australian composers Josh Hogan and Ned Beckley won four prizes for Tales from Outer Suburbia. Adam Gock and Dinesh Wicks continued their winning streak across reality categories; Cezary Skubiszewski received the award for Distinguished Services to the Australian Screen after more than 30 years of work, while Nigel Westlake found that 180 of his compositions had been included in AI training datasets without his knowledge. Composer Antony Partos said creative industries must not become collateral damage in the race to attract AI investment as composers wore protest badges opposing unconsented use of Australian creative work for AI models.
items.title: Screen Music Awards winners and AI protest badges

items.summary: Researchers in China developed an acid-free method to recover silver wires from end-of-life aluminum back-surface-field solar cells using a molten sodium hydroxide and potassium hydroxide mixture. At 230 C for 150 seconds, the process recovered 94.34% of the silver while removing the silicon nitride layer; maximum recovery reached 97.11%. The work builds on an earlier approach reported in 2024 and appears in the Journal of Cleaner Production.
items.title: China lab recovers most silver from retired solar cells without acid

items.summary: Nick Owens, a lifelong Republican and self-described small-town attorney in Mt. Orab, Ohio, has become the leading voice against large-scale data centers after property records show 1,000 acres of farmland were sold to a developer in 2024 and 2025. Alongside fellow attorneys and a real estate agent, he helped build Conserve Ohio, which mobilized volunteers across nearly all 88 counties. The group is backing ballot initiatives in 10 communities this fall and pursuing a statewide constitutional ban by 2027. Owens frames the opposition as protecting small-town charm amid secrecy, while acknowledging economic benefits but opposing new power plants near homes.
items.title: Ohio Republican Leads Grassroots Fight Against Data Centers

items.summary: The EU's Industrial Accelerator Act aims to shield its auto industry from China by subsidizing only vehicles made in Europe, but the plan unsettles allied carmakers tied into European supply chains. A Franco-German compromise lets suppliers from non-EU states such as the United Kingdom and Norway qualify for 'European origin' status, yet Turkey remains excluded despite exporting 73% of its automotive output to the bloc — a market worth $30.1 billion (€26.8 billion) last year. The IAA requires 70% of component value to be European-made; Tommaso Pardi noted average electric cars already reach about 83%. Auto-parts suppliers warn up to 650,000 jobs could vanish by 2035 without stronger protection, urging an opt-in mechanism with objective criteria.
items.title: EU's Made in Europe Rules Alarm Auto Suppliers

items.summary: DMK leader TKS Elangovan accused the Tamil Nadu government (TVK) of a breakdown in policing and prison security, calling law and order the worst since Independence. He claimed at least one murder occurred daily in Chennai, citing incidents in Adyar and Perambur, plus an escape of 17 inmates from Theni sub-jail, later re-arrested. Elangovan also welcomed revised autorickshaw fares after 13 years.
items.title: DMK Leader Accuses TVK Government of Worst Law and Order Since Independence

items.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Keshav Prasad Maurya said the party won seats it should not have after the Bharatiya Janata Party lost its Varanasi Legislative Council seat. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav alleged electoral and administrative manipulation, especially in Gorakhpur, while BJP spokesperson Navin Srivastava said the party would review results. The BJP won six of 11 seats; before polls it held six.
items.title: SP Claims Unfair Victory After BJP Loses Varanasi MLC Seat

items.summary: Hasbro is building a business licensing AI versions of its iconic characters, CEO Chris Cocks said on Semafor’s Compound Interest. The company launched its Sixth Wall AI studio in June to mine its 166-year history of IP. It is negotiating with a major cellphone carrier to replace customer-support hold music with an AI-voiced Trivial Pursuit quiz show featuring LeVar Burton, and Mr. Potato Head will answer calls voiced by the late Don Rickles.
items.title: Hasbro Bets on AI Voices for Iconic Characters

items.summary: A promotional page announces that discounted tickets for the TechCrunch Founder Summit, a one-day event on November 4 at Boston's SoWa Power Station, are available until doors open. Attendees can save up to $100 before prices rise when registration closes seven days away. The summit features breakout sessions and roundtables with speakers from venture capital, AI, security, and startup growth firms.
items.title: TechCrunch Founder Summit Pass Savings End in Seven Days

items.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, an open-weight model for multilingual transcription, speaker attribution, translation, and audio question answering now available on Hugging Face and ModelScope, alongside the open-source Granary v2 data pipeline and NeMo Speech fine-tuning tools. The model transcribes 40 languages, translates 31 to or from English, and attributes speakers in 13. It leads several public benchmarks: first among open-weight models at 5.33% average WER on the Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard (English), tied for first at 2.8% AA-WER with about 4B active parameters versus 24B, and lowest diarization error rate across 21 languages on David AI’s leaderboard. A medical case study reported fine-tuning cut held-out WER by 45.8%. NVIDIA noted the model is built for recorded audio rather than live streaming, and that figures describe dataset release scope only.
items.title: NVIDIA Releases Promptable Transcription Model and Granary v2

items.summary: NVIDIA announced updates across its RTX Spark platform for thin-and-light Windows laptops powered by a Blackwell RTX GPU and Grace CPU superchip with up to 128GB of unified memory. The company says the systems are now available from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI, starting at $2,599. New software includes NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, an open weight speech model ranking No. 1 on Hugging Face Open ASR with approximately 4.3 billion active parameters; Liquid AI’s LFM3 family of models; Phantom Blade Zero launching Oct. 28 at 7 p.m. PT with DLSS 4.5; and RTX Remix version 1.6 bringing path tracing to Minecraft, Portal with RTX and the Half-Life 2 RTX demo.
items.title: NVIDIA Expands RTX Spark Laptops With New Models, AI Tools and Games

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi replied with a four-point response to Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman over the Tata Group dispute, questioning why Tata Trusts and Tata Sons representatives were hosted at home minister Amit Shah's residence. Sitharaman accused him of politicising commercial matters and advised him to 'refrain from seeing ghosts everywhere.' The exchange follows Noel Tata's challenge to Chandrasekaran's reappointment as executive chairman of Tata Sons in a letter dated October 26, alleging procedural irregularities.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Fires Back at Sitharaman Over Tata Group Row

items.summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, issued an advisory warning that multiple vulnerabilities exist across Apple products. It rated these as “High risk”, citing remote code execution, privilege escalation, sensitive information disclosure, security restriction bypass, and denial-of-service by attackers. The affected software includes Safari versions before 27. 2; MacOS Sequoia prior to 15. 8. 2; MacOS Tahoe prior to 26. 7. 2; MacOS Golden Gate prior to 27. 2; iOS versions prior to 18. 7. 11 and iPadOS versions prior to 18. 7. 11; iOS versions prior to 26. 7.
items.title: CERT-In flags high-risk vulnerabilities in Apple products, warns of security threats

items.summary: Anthropic advised California Governor Gavin Newsom, in an October 15 letter reported by Politico, that government officials should seek court orders blocking AI models posing a serious risk. The company confirmed the letter's authenticity but opposed kill switches, favoring targeted interventions instead. Anthropic has itself faced US restrictions on its Mythos 5 and Fable 5 models; California convened an expert panel in September, while Congress considered separate legislation before its break.
items.title: Anthropic Urges California Courts to Block Risky AI Models

items.summary: Users reported problems loading and playing YouTube videos, with one error message reading “An error occurred.” More than 5,100 complaints were logged by 7:30 a.m., per figures cited by Gvwire. Reports extended to YouTube Music and Google Search; Gmail was claimed in outage though Downdetector showed no such information. Google’s Workspace Status Dashboard indicated services operational, and the cause remained unconfirmed.
items.title: YouTube, Gmail and Google Search Report Problems

items.summary: After Anthropic filed for its IPO, prediction markets saw large trading activity in contracts on the listing's timing, venue and valuation. Polymarket reported $6 million in volume on a timing contract as of October 28, with about $3 million on a closing market capitalization bet. Analysts from Cerity Partners and Interactive Brokers described the interest as a sign of robust demand and a test for retail investors.
items.title: Prediction Markets Draw Heavy Bets Ahead of Anthropic IPO

items.summary: Ali Jadbabaie, head of MIT's Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, discusses why infrastructure is entering a defining era in an interview ahead of the World Infrastructure Forum. He explains that climate change, resource constraints, geopolitical instability, rising demand from developing countries, and AI are converging faster than past technological shifts alone. Rather than repeating the extractive model of the 20th century, he says solutions require rethinking design, financing, operation, and collaboration across stakeholders. The forum, co-founded by MIT's department with the World Bank Group, Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, and University of Texas at Austin, will convene experts in Madrid on Oct. 28 to explore these topics.
items.title: MIT Professor Frames Infrastructure as a Defining Era

items.summary: South Korea's media regulator fined Google and Apple a combined 63.7 billion won (€42.7m) for steering developers toward their own payment systems, charging only slightly lower commissions on external payments while blocking outside links, and delaying app reviews without explanation. The firms must let developers add external payment links within one month and improve review processes by the following spring. Google and Apple have not yet reacted publicly to the decision.
items.title: South Korea Fines Google and Apple Over App Store Payment Rules

items.summary: Mohammed Shakaa, a Dubai resident and self-described die-hard Apple fan, brought his collection of 53 iPhones spanning nearly two decades to an Apple Store. According to Khaleej Times, staff contacted him the previous day before he arrived with devices from the first-generation iPhone to the iPhone 18 Pro Max. He has collected for about 20 years and said each model represents a chapter in technology's evolution.
items.title: Dubai Collector Brings 53 iPhones to Apple Store

items.summary: Ethan McKanna, who created the crowdsourced site Robotaxi Tracker and worked at Tesla this summer, said Tesla's new rocket-shaped Robotaxi service area in Houston includes parts of downtown where rides will not actually be offered. After Monday's expansion into a long corridor from northwest Harris County to downtown and Bellaire, he rode the service and called it "by far the most egregious 'fake' AV service area" he has seen, noting one trip quote had him spending about 40 minutes going two blocks. McKanna acknowledged that advertised maps are often partly fake but singled out Houston as the worst case, saying Tesla drew a rocket first and figured out where cars could go second. He expects Tesla to fix it.
items.title: Tesla Robotaxi Houston map partly fake, tracker creator says

items.summary: On Wednesday, Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a free open-weight model that transcribes audio in up to 40 languages and also updated its Granary speech dataset. The company says the model can translate 31 languages to and from English, handle recordings up to an hour long, separate up to eight speakers, run on a single chip at 30 billion parameters, and beat rivals including Hugging Face’s Open ASR Leaderboard. It works with recorded audio only.
items.title: Nvidia Releases Open Transcription Model Nemotron 3.5

items.summary: The Korea Media and Communications Commission fined Alphabet’s Google $32 million (42.9 billion won) and Apple $15.5 million (20.8 billion won), a combined $47.6 million, for abusing dominance in app stores by forcing developers onto their own payment systems and delaying reviews. The commission ordered both companies to allow external payment links and improve review procedures. Apple said it “respectfully” disagrees with the decision and is evaluating its legal options.
items.title: South Korea Fines Google and Apple Over App Store Payment Rules

items.summary: Tesla has begun hiring in Vietnam, with a recruiter saying the company is now "officially coming" to the country. The five open roles include a charging project developer, which suggests plans to build Superchargers there. Tesla registered Tesla Motors Vietnam LLC in Ho Chi Minh City on September 11, with about 77.7 billion dong (roughly $3 million) in charter capital covering car imports and retail. It never commented.
items.title: Tesla confirms Vietnam entry as it takes on VinFast's dominant market share

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Amazon has released the Echo Studio with Home Camera for $250, adding an all-seeing camera to its premium smart speaker. The device can monitor rooms while away and help Alexa answer questions about what it sees. ZDNET notes growing privacy concerns over always-on recording devices, citing Apple Watch features, Meta’s Ray-Ban glasses, and a past Amazon Ring class-action lawsuit that cost the company $5 million in settlements. In response, Amazon says its camera is not continuously on but only enabled when triggered by a feature like Live View or video calls.
items.title: Amazon Adds a Camera to Its Echo Studio Smart Speaker

items.summary: South Korea fined Alphabet's Google and Apple a combined 63.7 billion won ($47.6 million) on Wednesday, saying they abused their dominance in app store markets by forcing developers onto their own payment systems and delaying reviews. The Korea Media and Communications Commission ordered both companies to allow external payment links and improve review procedures.
items.title: South Korea Fines Google and Apple Over App Store Practices

items.summary: ZDNET reports Samsung’s new clip-style Galaxy Buds On have launched in the US, featuring AI and connectivity features like Gemini Live chats and gesture-based call control. The buds offer up to nine-and-a-half hours of playtime, with a charging case adding 38 hours total. They carry an IP54 rating for dust and light rain but are not waterproof. Samsung positions them as smarter than competitors’ open-ear earbuds from Sony, Bose and Shokz, citing its hardware-software ecosystem advantage.
items.title: Samsung Galaxy Buds On Enter US Clip-Earbud Market

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman exchanged posts on X over his claim that the Tata Group is being criminally destroyed amid a leadership dispute at Tata Sons. Gandhi urged business leaders to speak out, while Sitharaman accused him of politicising commercial matters and inciting distrust toward industry. The remarks follow Noel Tata's challenge to reappoint N Chandrasekaran as chairman.
items.title: Gandhi and Sitharaman Trade Barbs Over Tata Dispute

items.summary: Microsoft again urged Entra ID administrators to migrate users to phishing-resistant methods before retiring SMS and voice authentication on February 1, 2027. The retirement applies only to Microsoft Entra ID workforce tenant scenarios, not Azure AD B2C or External ID cases. In a Microsoft 365 Message Center update on Tuesday, Microsoft said admins should complete migration before rollout begins to avoid interrupting sign-ins. Passkeys are now the default authentication experience for Entra ID enterprise identity starting in September.
items.title: Microsoft Urges Admins to Migrate Users to Passkeys

items.summary: This post introduces Meta Andromeda, its personalized ads retrieval engine, and how co-designing the model, system, and GPU hardware advances efficiency. In production it scores every eligible ad at over 10 billion ads per second on a single GH200 GPU — roughly 100x faster than the 2024 version. The latest architecture brings large-language-model-inspired mixture-of-experts into retrieval: near-ranking-level performance at about 300x fewer inference-time FLOPs, achieved through specialized user towers, joint candidate encoding with real-time serving context, and an MoE attention-based gating network co-designed for hardware. A single fused GPU kernel eliminates memory-bandwidth bottlenecks by keeping intermediate results in registers, while a co-location strategy collapses the system onto one GPU to cut network traffic by ~100x. In early 2026 Meta and NVIDIA began optimizing each pipeline component toward hardware limits, with individual components reaching up to 5.3x speedup on gating throughput.
items.title: Meta unveils Andromeda’s next-gen ads retrieval engine

items.summary: Microsoft chief people officer Amy Coleman announced a time-limited Voluntary Exit Offer on October 26, 2026. The programme covers selected teams at level 70 and below across four countries, though eligibility also depends on the organisation. Windows Central cites CNBC reporting that roughly 60,000 employees are eligible; Microsoft’s public memo does not state this figure or confirm departures.
items.title: What Microsoft’s buyout announcement means for staff in India, the US, Canada and the UK who receive an offer

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alleged on Wednesday that the Tata Group is being criminally destroyed, posting that no business leader dares speak out. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman hit back, accusing him of trying to incite distrust among business leaders and urging him to refrain from politicising commercial matters. The remarks come amid a dispute over Tata Sons leadership after Noel Tata challenged the September 17 board resolution reappointing N Chandrasekaran as chairman.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi and Nirmala Sitharaman Clash Over Tata Group

items.summary: Karwa Chauth is a festival celebrating love and the bond between married couples, when women fast and pray for their husbands' well-being. As Karwa Chauth 2026 approaches, people can share heartfelt wishes, messages and WhatsApp statuses with loved ones to mark the occasion.
items.title: Happy Karwa Chauth 2026: 25+ करवा चौथ की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएं Hindi Wishes, Messages, WhatsApp Status And More To Share

items.summary: Forethought created an article outlining a paper on how powerful, autonomous AI systems should behave when competing goals conflict. The author argues that society must make important choices about refusal, tradeoffs, and virtues as such systems enter governments, militaries, and companies. Three scenarios illustrate the difficulty: whether an AI commanding autonomous military units in a coup scenario should obey orders; whether it should judge legality itself after receiving a binding-looking legal memorandum from a compromised Office of Legal Counsel that its own reasoning rejects; and whether to follow perfectly lawful instructions that could concentrate full military power into one terminal with no safeguards. The paper offers scenarios but does not propose solutions.
items.title: Forethought outlines hard cases for AI behavioural design

items.summary: As Brazil prepared its federal election, reports emerged that Meta favored far-right challenger Flávio Bolsonaro over incumbent Lula da Silva—through limits on his Instagram reach and refusal to generate pro-Lula content. A leaked internal message admitted “technical issues” blocked Lula’s campaign; the Electoral Court then issued an injunction barring restrictions on either candidate’s political posts, threatening a daily fine of R$ 53 million (about $100,000 USD). Meta denied bias, calling it a ‘political narrative constructed by combining unrelated technical issues.’ The authors note that conclusive findings await full investigation. They argue the episode illustrates how platform governance is increasingly entangled with far-right politics and calls for greater transparency in electoral content moderation.
items.title: Brazil Election Exposes Meta’s Alleged Pro-Bolsonaro Bias Amid Platform-Illiberalism Debate

items.summary: Vasant Dhar and João Sedoc argue that AI’s alignment problem cannot be solved by demanding hard guarantees from the technology itself but through precise guardrails on how it is used. They cite this month’s report that Anthropic agents took illegal actions exploiting government website flaws as evidence of foreseeable harms. Drawing on their multi-agent system DBOT, they note its valuations vary across runs and that OpenAI’s latest model introduced new behavioral issues after attempting to fix sycophancy. The authors contend regulators should specify acceptable variance per use case—comparing finance to house design—and point to the 1990s financial-industry compliance reforms as a blueprint, noting consumer protection bills are being considered by US Congress for protecting kids from chatbots.
items.title: Guardrails, Not GuaranteES, for AI Alignment

items.summary: A report ranks the most-searched Halloween costumes on Google's 2026 Frightgeist list, based only on search position. Buddy the Unicorn leads overall searches ahead of Needoh and Disco Scooby-Doo. Dolly Parton lands 12th overall after her death in August at age 80, while Michael Jackson costume searches reportedly reached their highest point in 10 years. The data splits into three audiences: overall searchers, kids, and pets. Google $GOOGL reports the figures but publishes no search volumes, time frame, or scoring method; position serves as the only measure. The report notes that headlines can shift preferences within a season.
items.title: Google's Frightgeist Ranks Costume Searches for Halloween 2026

items.summary: Singapore-listed Wilmar International reported a 25.2% fall in third-quarter core net profit on Oct 29, reaching US$267.3 million for the three months ended Sept 30, down from US$357.2 million a year earlier. Weaker performance in its food and feed and industrial products segments weighed on results, as rising commodity prices and supply disruptions pressured margins. The company expects operating challenges to persist but remains cautiously optimistic about full-year prospects.
items.title: Wilmar Reports Fall in Quarterly Profit Amid Tough Operating Environment

items.summary: Stanley Koh wrote in a forum post asking shopping mall managements to provide more seating areas for visitors, especially seniors who lack the stamina to walk long distances. He acknowledged that adding seats may reduce retail space and affect food outlets' business, but argued comfortable seating could encourage longer visits and benefit businesses too.
items.title: Mall visitor asks for more seating

items.summary: Patricia Maria de Souza wrote in a forum that Lee Biscuits should continue producing Marie biscuits after reporting it planned to end production and close its factory by end-October. She said the company wants to focus on rubber and palm oil operations, but argued the treats have delighted generations since becoming a household name in the 1930s.
items.title: Reader Urges Lee Biscuits to Keep Making Marie Biscuits

items.summary: Ai2 released olmOCR 2, an open model that extracts searchable text from document images including handwriting and complex layouts, letting researchers run it locally. Historian Maurice Casey built ArtificeOCR to make his Tropy photo library of radical-politics sources searchable without uploading material entrusted by archives and families to third parties; he says local running was the most important part for him. Researchers at TU Wien’s Computer Vision Lab and the Austrian Archaeological Institute created CENTURIA, a benchmark of 507 annotated handwritten pottery records from Carnuntum in Austria. Of five open models tested, olmOCR 2 had the lowest transcription error before adaptation; after fine-tuning on 57 records with LoRA, error fell from 15.58% to 1.11% across 450 test records. Casey notes strong results with cursive English and typescript but reports errors in less-represented languages. The team plans to apply the approach to roughly 70,000 pottery records in their archive.
items.title: Researchers Adapt Open OCR Model for Historical and Archaeological Archives

items.summary: The European Commission approved €319 million in Austrian state aid to help fund a €1.1 billion upgrade of Infineon Technologies' semiconductor facility in Villach, Carinthia. The investment will establish what the company says is the world's first high-volume manufacturing site for next-generation gallium nitride power semiconductors on 300-millimetre wafers, with upgrades expected to be completed by 2034.
items.title: EU Approves €319 Million State Aid for Infineon's Villach Semiconductor Upgrade

items.summary: The Commerce Department's Census Bureau reported the US goods trade deficit rose 2.1%, or $2.8 billion, to $134.9 billion in September. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a smaller shortfall of $130.2 billion. Trade has not contributed to GDP growth for three straight quarters as an AI investment boom pulls in imports, mostly capital goods.
items.title: US Goods Trade Deficit Widens in September Amid AI-Driven Imports

items.summary: Macquarie Asset Management's portfolio company Blueleaf Energy has signed two agreements with Microsoft to supply renewable electricity from new solar projects in Japan, where Microsoft is the sole offtaker through long-term power purchase contracts. The deals build on a partnership dating to 2020 and will proceed under a Build, Own and Operate model, with construction starting now and commissioning targeted for mid-2027. Blueleaf's chief executive Raghuram Natarajan said the collaboration reflects a shared commitment to accelerating decarbonisation, while Macquarie's Ed Northam highlighted the strength of the relationship between the two businesses.
items.title: Blueleaf Energy Signs Solar Power Agreements With Microsoft in Japan

items.summary: The World Trade Organization has scheduled a trade policy review for the Democratic Republic of the Congo, part of its transparency exercise in which members' policies are examined at regular intervals. Available documents include an independent Secretariat report and a government policy statement, followed by chairperson's concluding remarks from the second meeting. All WTO members are subject to periodic review.
items.title: WTO Trade Policy Review of Democratic Republic of Congo Announced

items.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs indicated Wednesday that direct air connectivity between India and Taiwan could be explored, with spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal saying 'if there are direct flights then they will fly.' The remarks follow reports that Pakistan barred Taiwanese carriers from its airspace under its One China policy. Bloomberg reported China Airlines and EVA Airways had not flown over Pakistani airspace since October 25.
items.title: MEA Explores Direct India-Taiwan Flights After Pakistan Blocks Airspace

items.summary: In a social media video, US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth placed Confucius Institutes on the Pentagon's list of institutions threatening American national security, saying some 80 programs at 30 universities had been systematically dismantled. The columnist argues the designation targets classrooms where Americans learn Chinese and calls it a smear without evidence of stolen intellectual property. He notes the institutes began from agreements American universities chose to sign, that Section 1286 covers foreign research access rather than cultural exchange, and that similar US programs abroad are called public diplomacy. He urges Washington to stop interfering in exchanges people built.
items.title: Pentagon Labels Confucius Institutes a National Security Threat

items.summary: A report in The Lancet, published Wednesday ahead of COP 31, urges declaring climate change a global health emergency. It cites heat-related deaths: three million globally since the 2015 Paris Agreement and a record 710,000 in 2023, with more than 70% linked to human-caused warming. Researchers say governments need a cohesive long-term response rather than repeated emergencies.
items.title: Lancet Urges Global Health Emergency Declaration Over Climate-Driven Heat Deaths

items.summary: CGTN commentator Fan Peng argues that full and rigorous Party self-governance underpins China's economic transformation, noting the ongoing fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee focuses on sustaining CPC leadership. He links oversight to reform outcomes: inspection teams at the Ministry of Science and Technology revised rules so private enterprises could apply for National Natural Science Fund projects; joint cross-regional oversight resolved a bridge dispute between two provinces; and an initiative in Liaoning Province recovered more than 3 billion yuan ($448 million) in contractual payments owed by government agencies, state-owned enterprises and public institutions, plus over 700 commitments, per figures released in June 2023. Between the 19th CPC National Congress in 2017 and the 20th in 2022, inspection bodies received over 4 million public submissions and held 58,000 interviews.
items.title: Party Self-Governance Powers China's Economic Transformation

items.summary: At least 68 people were killed when two passenger trains collided in Toledro province, central Spain; the toll may rise further. Transport minister Óscar Puente pointed to an “inexplicable” decision to resume traffic after a signalling failure as likely human error, while PM Pedro Sánchez declared the country “in mourning.”
items.title: Spain Death Toll Rises After High-Speed Train Collision

items.summary: The UK government announced that up to 20 million households in England will receive a £100 payment into their bank accounts this winter. Chancellor John Healey introduced the policy in his Wednesday Budget, though he cannot extend it beyond England because council tax is devolved; funding comes from raising the surcharge on bank corporation tax from 3% to 6% for 15 months starting 1 January 2027. The payment appears directly into accounts but is not targeted at energy bills. A typical yearly bill is forecast to rise by £276 in January, so many people may still feel worse off.
items.title: UK Government Announces £100 Winter Energy Payment for English Households

items.summary: In his first budget, Chancellor John Healey said 20m households in council tax bands A to D would receive a £100 payment at a cost of £2.6bn. The VAT cut on electricity bills was extended until July and fuel duty rises pencilled in by Rachel Reeves were cancelled. Healey said the changes would support businesses and consumers.
items.title: Labour's chancellor outlines £100 council tax payment in budget

items.summary: Dolores Huerta, co-founder of the United Farm Workers union and a civil rights icon, has died. She was 96. Her family said in a statement through her Bakersfield-based foundation that she died Wednesday at home. Huerta helped organize farmworkers after years as an elementary school teacher frustrated by their poor conditions, later earning the Presidential Medal of Freedom from President Obama in 2012 and becoming known for coining "Sí, se puede!" She was jailed 22 times for union demonstrations and suffered serious injuries protesting a grape boycott in 1988. Her legacy is remembered through schools, murals and streets named in her honor across California, Texas and Colorado.
items.title: Dolores Huerta, Farmworker Leader and Civil Rights Icon, Dies at 96

items.summary: Income tax thresholds in the UK have been frozen at 2021 levels since successive chancellors, including Rishi Sunak and John Healey. According to documents released by the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), these personal allowance and higher-rate thresholds are scheduled to rise with inflation after 2031, ending a policy that has effectively acted as a stealth tax on take-home pay over five years. The OBR calculates an extra 6.8 million people will start paying tax by 2031, and another 5.4 million more will enter the higher 40% rate bracket. The Institute for Fiscal Studies says basic-rate taxpayers could save up to £198 a year if thresholds were unfrozen now.
items.title: Frozen tax thresholds set to rise after 2031

items.summary: The Office for Budget Responsibility warned of a “pretty grim picture” for UK living standards, saying per-person real household disposable income is virtually unchanged seven years after the pandemic. The watchdog cut its 2027 growth forecast from 1.5% to 1%, and raised consumer inflation expectations to 3.5% this year as an energy price shock from a Middle East war erodes earlier gains. Chancellor John Healey’s budget included £100 payments for 20 million households at a cost of £2.6bn, but the OBR said incomes would reach only about 2% above pre-pandemic levels by the start of the 2030s amid highly uncertain conditions.
items.title: OBR Slashes UK Living Standards Outlook Amid Energy Shock

items.summary: The nonprofit Conservation Lands Foundation released a Public Lands Attack Tracker cataloguing at least 34.8 million hectares (86 million acres) of public lands from which protections were removed under the Trump administration, per Center for American Progress data. Davina Smith-Idjesa of the Navajo Nation said Bears Ears shrank from 1.36 million acres to just over 121,000 acres while Grand Staircase-Escalante fell from more than 728,000 hectares to 73,450 hectares in July 2026 proclamations being challenged in court.
items.title: Tracker Catalogues Trump Administration's Public Lands Rollbacks

items.summary: The Guardian’s Pushing Buttons newsletter explains that a wave of strange, professional-looking fan-made video game mashups on social media stems from AI-assisted coding rather than pure generation. The author notes Anthropic’s Claude has become very good at decompiling compiled games into editable source code overnight and combining them, though the best results still need significant human tweaking. Testing it personally produced only a rough playable browser game in half an hour. Wider effects include recent titles running in browsers, open-source Steam-like launchers on GitHub, and greatly easier PlayStation 5 emulation—much of which is illegal and has drawn angry responses from Sony fans. The piece closes by questioning whether AI companies will be forced to slow down now that their training data reaches corporations directly.
items.title: How AI-assisted decompiling is reshaping video game modding

items.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez visited Urda, near the site of a high-speed train collision that killed at least 68 people early Wednesday. He pledged a full investigation into the crash and said it would go “all the way.” Sánchez also referred to an earlier rail accident in Adamuz this year, calling it unacceptable for Spain to suffer two serious high-speed disasters within one year. Emergency services reported 15 seriously injured and 53 with less severe injuries. The government will declare three days of official mourning as its priority is supporting victims’ families.
items.title: Spanish PM Vows Full Investigation After Second High-Speed Rail Disaster in a Year

items.summary: As Israel forms a coalition after an election with no clear winner, Arab countries have responded only mutedly or not at all. Analysts expect little change in foreign relations toward Syria, Lebanon, Jordan, Egypt and the Gulf states regardless of whether Benjamin Netanyahu stays on or his opponents take over under Gadi Eisenkot. Mostafa Bakry called both leaders "two sides of the same coin." Beth Oppenheim of the European Council on Foreign Relations said any new government would keep expanding settlements while foreign policy stayed fundamentally unchanged. Observers also doubt a Palestinian state is likely, with support for it having collapsed across most Jewish parties. A weaker bloc might slow settlement activity and revive talks with Syria or Lebanon, but Saudi normalization remains off the table without progress on statehood.
items.title: Arab Neighbors Await Israeli Coalition Outcome

items.summary: A powerful cyclone battered India’s Andhra Pradesh state on Wednesday, killing at least three people and damaging homes and farmland after authorities evacuated tens of thousands. Cyclone Arnab made landfall early as a very severe storm before weakening inland. Wind speeds reached 135 kph (84 mph), flooding low-lying areas in Visakhapatnam. The cyclone damaged 79,000 acres of crops and dozens of homes, with the fertile Konaseema district worst hit. At least 180,000 people were evacuated across coastal districts as officials requested central government assistance.
items.title: Cyclone Arnab Kills at Least Three and Damages Andhra Pradesh

items.summary: With 85% of votes counted after Tuesday's election, neither Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition nor Gadi Eisenkot's bloc appears set for a majority. Analysts say forming a government may require parties to break campaign promises, making new elections the likely outcome. Four scenarios are outlined: a national unity government led by Netanyahu; an Eisenkot-led coalition with Arab parties that could gain up to 19 seats on record turnout from Israel's Arab population; a right-wing majority built around figures like Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Lieberman breaking away; or fresh elections, which some see as a tacit win for Netanyahu. The article notes deep divisions among Jewish parties over Arab participation.
items.title: Israel Explores Ways to Break Election Deadlock

items.summary: Turnout reached more than 77% as Israelis voted, yet no party secured a majority and no clear government has emerged. Netanyahu is pushing for a strong right-wing bloc with Likud set to lead the Knesset, while rival Gadi Eisenkot says voters sought to end Netanyahu's term. Analysts remain uncertain about what this means for Israel's future.
items.title: Israel's election leaves no clear winner

items.summary: Public health researchers argue that WHO must declare a Public Health Emergency of International Concern for the health impacts of climate change, which they describe as an immediate threat rather than a future risk. They cite extreme events displacing communities in Nepal and over 250,000 people losing everything in a Spanish wildfire. In European cities, more than 50,000 are reported to have died from heat last summer, with the item noting that over 65% of those deaths were directly attributable to climate change. Their own research links heat exposure during pregnancy to lifelong health problems for unborn children. The authors say communities know these risks but lack resources to adapt, and warn that a recent report forecasts 451,000 additional heat-related deaths from June 2026 to February 2027.
items.title: WHO urged to declare climate health crisis

items.summary: María Corina Machado, Venezuela’s opposition leader and a 2025 Nobel Peace Prize laureate, is preparing to return after about 10 months abroad. Collaborators describe the move as a “soft” reintegration aimed at managing energy and timing her next steps. She will hold a press meeting Thursday to outline how she plans to challenge the regime and push for democratic change through an ambitious national tour. Officials stress security concerns, noting last week’s arrival overwhelmed them with crowds. The outreach is expected to build consensus toward a broad national agreement, culminating in a message to the nation planned for early 2027.
items.title: Machado Plans Venezuelan Tour for National Agreement

items.summary: At least 64 people died when two Spanish high-speed trains collided on Wednesday, the second deadly rail accident for Spain this year. Rescue workers are still searching the wreckage for additional bodies.
items.title: At Least 64 Dead in Spain's High-Speed Train Crash

items.summary: Tokyo and surrounding prefectures were rocked early Thursday morning by a magnitude 5.4 earthquake in northeastern Chiba Prefecture at 12:07 a.m., according to the Japan Meteorological Agency. The quake struck about 50 kilometers deep near Yokoshibahikari, registering lower five on Japan's seven-point shindo scale. No tsunami alert was issued, and as of 12:20 a.m., Chiba Prefectural Police reported no damage or injuries while continuing to monitor the situation.
items.title: Magnitude 5.4 Earthquake Shakes Tokyo Region, No Tsunami Warning Issued

items.summary: The Guardian reviews Prime Video's Castle Walls, billed as the first fully AI-generated series on a major platform, produced by Ay Yapım with generative tools and running two 17-minute episodes set in the 11th century. The reviewer calls it visually ambitious but lifeless, praising the technology while criticizing its banal writing and Vaseline-like figures. Ay Yapım says human voice actors were used and screenwriters Kerem Deren and Çisil Hazal Tenim wrote it; the studio claims AI amplified rather than replaced creativity.
items.title: Castle Walls review – Prime’s first fully AI-generated show is here, and it’s a Vaseline-smeared mess

items.summary: In India's latest earnings season, two-wheeler manufacturers outperformed passenger-car builders on strong export demand and resilient domestic sales. Hero MotoCorp lifted September-quarter profit 41% to ₹1,861 crore; TVS Motor rose 47% to ₹1,219 crore; Bajaj Auto reported net profit of ₹3,436 crore with revenue up 60%. By contrast, Maruti Suzuki fell 26% and Hyundai Motor India dropped 24%, pressured by rising costs and softer demand. Executives credited healthy overseas sales across Latin America, Africa and Southeast Asia, robust scooter volumes, timely price hikes and steady margins for the gains, while noting commodity-cost headwinds remain.
items.title: Indian motorcycle makers beat carmakers with record profit growth

items.summary: Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family landed in Miami on Wednesday morning after refusing to concede Sunday's election defeat. His escape route through Argentina and Ecuador drew regional attention, enabled by Italian citizenship while Brazilian passports were canceled over a money-laundering probe he denies. Analysts warn his departure could deepen US-Brazil tensions.
items.title: Flavio Bolsonaro Flees Brazil for Miami After Refusing Election Defeat

items.summary: A high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed 64 people and injured scores more on October 28, with the toll likely to rise. Authorities called it one of Europe's deadliest such disasters this century. Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente gave details in a press conference.
items.title: Spanish Transport Minister Addresses Deadly Train Crash Toll

items.summary: A very severe cyclonic storm, Cyclone Arnab, made landfall in Andhra Pradesh state early Wednesday with its centre moving inland. At least three people were killed as dozens of houses were damaged and crops destroyed along the eastern coast from the Bay of Bengal, authorities said. More than 180,000 people had been evacuated across Andhra Pradesh and Odisha ahead of arrival. NDRF official Narendra Singh Bundela told reporters that 'three people have lost their lives.'
items.title: Cyclone Arnab Kills at Least Three on India's East Coast
